a186.speaker: Bill Gates, Microsoft founder and philanthropist (blog post)
a186.name: Bill Gates
a186.title: Microsoft founder and philanthropist (blog post)
a186.speech: Said he intends to give away 99% of his vast fortune over the next 20 years and would accelerate his giving via his foundation, with plans to end its operations in 2045: "People will say a lot of things about me when I die, but I am determined that 'he died rich' will not be one of them" ; said his foundation has already given $100bn towards health and development projects, and that he expects it will spend another $200bn, depending on markets and inflation, over the next two decades.

a186.speaker: Bill Gates (interview with the BBC's Newshour)
a186.name: Bill Gates (interview with the BBC's Newshour)
a186.speech: Told the BBC's Newshour that there will be other wealthy people in 20 years who can better tackle future challenges: "It's really about the urgency. We can spend a lot more if we're not trying to be perpetual, and I know that the spending will be in line with my values."

a186.speaker: Andrew Carnegie, tycoon (1889 essay 'The Gospel of Wealth', quoted by Gates)
a186.name: Andrew Carnegie
a186.title: tycoon (1889 essay 'The Gospel of Wealth', quoted by Gates)
a186.speech: Mr Gates quoted Mr Carnegie, who wrote: "The man who dies thus rich dies disgraced." The essay argues that wealthy people have a duty to return their fortunes to society.

a186.speaker: Bill Gates (blog post)
a186.name: Bill Gates (blog post)
a186.speech: Outlined three main goals for his foundation: eliminating preventable diseases which kill mothers and children; eliminating infectious diseases including malaria and measles; and eliminating poverty for hundreds of millions of people.

a186.speaker: Bill Gates (blog post)
a186.name: Bill Gates (blog post)
a186.speech: Criticised the US, UK and France for cutting their foreign aid budgets: "It's unclear whether the world's richest countries will continue to stand up for its poorest people. But the one thing we can guarantee is that, in all of our work, the Gates Foundation will support efforts to help people and countries pull themselves out of poverty."

a186.speaker: Bill Gates (interview with the BBC's Newshour)
a186.name: Bill Gates (interview with the BBC's Newshour)
a186.speech: On cuts to US aid made by the Department of Government Efficiency (Doge): "These cuts will kill not just children, but millions of children" ; "You wouldn't have expected the world's richest person to do it" ; "I'm disappointed that [Musk] made abrupt cuts and characterised them in a way that was unfair, including saying that, money was being spent in Gaza when in fact, it was money to prevent mothers from infecting their babies with HIV" ; "I mean, this is serious stuff."

a186.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a186.name: Donald Trump
a186.title: US President
a186.speech: Erroneously claimed that cancelled grants to a hospital in Gaza Province, Mozambique, were funding condoms "for Hamas" in the Gaza Strip.

a186.speaker: Elon Musk
a186.name: Elon Musk
a186.speech: Mr Musk later acknowledged the claim was wrong and said "we will make mistakes", however the cost-cutting continued.

a186.speaker: Critics of the Gates Foundation
a186.name: Critics of the Gates Foundation
a186.speech: Critics of his foundation say Mr Gates uses its charitable status to avoid tax and that it has undue influence over the global health system.

a186.speaker: Bloomberg (data cited)
a186.name: Bloomberg (data cited)
a186.speech: According to Bloomberg, the Microsoft founder is the fifth-richest person in the world.

a186.speaker: Elon Musk (non-response)
a186.name: Elon Musk (non-response)
a186.speech: The BBC has contacted Mr Musk for comment.

a220.speaker: Luis Munana, Namibian reality TV star and entrepreneur (Young, Famous & African)
a220.name: Luis Munana
a220.title: Namibian reality TV star and entrepreneur (Young, Famous & African)
a220.speech: Said he had sex with a fellow contestant in the Big Brother house. "I come from an extremely religious background," he says in part of a conversation with co-star Andile Ncube. "Upon coming out [of the Big Brother house], I got excommunicated from the congregation."

a220.speaker: Luis Munana, Namibian reality TV star and entrepreneur (Young, Famous & African)
a220.name: Luis Munana
a220.title: Namibian reality TV star and entrepreneur (Young, Famous & African)
a220.speech: Says it was seven going on eight years since his ex-communication from the church. "We don't communicate unless someone is ill or dying," he tells News24 in an interview. "But I do know they love me, and I love them."

a220.speaker: Luis Munana, Namibian reality TV star and entrepreneur (Young, Famous & African)
a220.name: Luis Munana
a220.title: Namibian reality TV star and entrepreneur (Young, Famous & African)
a220.speech: Without naming the religious organisation his family belongs to, says it has specific rules it abides by, and if you break them, you are reprimanded and given a chance to "repent" and change your ways; says members of the organisation are meant to "lead by example". "If we do things like going on national TV and having sex, it's a taboo," he says. "I was given a chance to say that I could leave that life behind and, by that, anything considered worldly. But, aside from that incident on Big Brother Africa, I did other things that are considered worldly."

a220.speaker: Luis Munana, Namibian reality TV star and entrepreneur (Young, Famous & African)
a220.name: Luis Munana
a220.title: Namibian reality TV star and entrepreneur (Young, Famous & African)
a220.speech: Says because of the ex-communication, anyone who is baptised into or has taken an oath or vow to the organisation, including family and friends, may not have contact with him. "I'm not allowed to socialise with anybody who is part of the organisation; I'm not allowed to step into the homes or be in their presence," he says. "That also means that I cannot go to my childhood home, and I cannot go to my siblings' homes because they are still active members of the organisation."

a220.speaker: Luis Munana, Namibian reality TV star and entrepreneur (Young, Famous & African)
a220.name: Luis Munana
a220.title: Namibian reality TV star and entrepreneur (Young, Famous & African)
a220.speech: Admits in the show that he does miss them, and there is a lot he wishes to share with them. "I know they don't have any ill feelings towards me, and I don't have any ill feelings towards them," he says as the interview ends. "They are just part of an organisation with rules, mandates and bylaws, which I was part of, but I left. They must abide by that; otherwise, they also risk being excommunicated, and I don't want that for them."

a324.speaker: Major General Abdoulaye Maïga, Mali's Minister of Territorial Administration
a324.name: Major General Abdoulaye Maïga
a324.title: Mali's Minister of Territorial Administration
a324.speech: Declared in his address that “it is essential to rethink international cooperation in the Sahel in depth in order to make it relevant in the face of contemporary realities,” and that the meeting is “a precious opportunity to share ideas, exchange experiences and build together a promising future for the States and the peoples of the Sahel.”

a324.speaker: Abdoulaye Diop, Mali's Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation
a324.name: Abdoulaye Diop
a324.title: Mali's Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation
a324.speech: Spoke of a reconfiguration of international cooperation, long based on development aid: “This reconfiguration begins on the basis of the three principles that we have put forward. Until now, cooperation with the countries of the Sahel, or cooperation with Mali, has been based on what is called development aid” ; “But one cannot develop on the basis of aid,” stating that it is necessary to leave this framework and enter into win-win partnership frameworks.

a377.speaker: Rwanda (Rwandan Paralympic body)
a377.name: Rwanda (Rwandan Paralympic body)
a377.speech: Has revealed it is aiming to send its largest ever Paralympic team to Rio 2016.

a453.speaker: Pericles, general of Ancient Greece and leader of Athens
a453.name: Pericles
a453.title: general of Ancient Greece and leader of Athens
a453.speech: “Just because you do not take an interest in politics, [it] doesn’t mean politics won’t take an interest in you.”

a453.speaker: Yuval Noah Harari (Prof.), historian and author of “Sapiens: A Brief History of Humankind”
a453.name: Yuval Noah Harari (Prof.)
a453.title: historian and author of “Sapiens: A Brief History of Humankind”
a453.speech: Thinks that the conflict will impact long-term budgeting priorities for Western countries: military budgets will rise substantially (case in point is Germany doubling its military budget) and less money will be spent on humanitarian causes.

a453.speaker: Yuval Noah Harari (Prof.), historian and author of “Sapiens: A Brief History of Humankind”
a453.name: Yuval Noah Harari (Prof.)
a453.title: historian and author of “Sapiens: A Brief History of Humankind”
a453.speech: Made the point that when Vladimir Putin, president of Russia, decided to invade the largest country in Eastern Europe, he united the whole West against himself.

a453.speaker: Ian Bremmer, American political analyst and head of The Eurasia Group
a453.name: Ian Bremmer
a453.title: American political analyst and head of The Eurasia Group
a453.speech: Describes the potential outcome of the Russian war and tough Western sanctions imposed on Russia as distinct in three ways: Russia will be much weakened economically; China will emerge as its senior partner in trade, buying resources for cheap and supplying manufactured goods for a premium; and the Russian economy will be completely disconnected from the West.

a453.speaker: Three researchers from the European Centre for Development Policy Management, Dutch think-tank (discussion paper on European and Chinese investments in Africa)
a453.name: Three researchers from the European Centre for Development Policy Management
a453.title: Dutch think-tank (discussion paper on European and Chinese investments in Africa)
a453.speech: Recently published a discussion paper comparing the EU’s ‘Global Gateway Initiative’ and China’s ‘Belt and Road Initiative’, showing China far ahead with 153 billion dollars in loans committed to African countries compared to a mere 11 billion euros of Official Development Assistance provided by Europe ; stress an important difference between Chinese and Western programmes, the latter’s international development model being built upon invasive conditionalities and reform requirements, an ‘instructional’ approach expanded also to the SDGs ; see a geographical rebalancing of Chinese overseas finance towards its more direct neighbourhood in East and West Asia.

a453.speaker: Ursula von der Leyen, president of the European Commission
a453.name: Ursula von der Leyen
a453.title: president of the European Commission
a453.speech: Announced that the Global Gateway Initiative will amount to 300 billion euros.

a453.speaker: Amy Myers Jaffe, managing director of the Climate Policy Lab at Tufts University
a453.name: Amy Myers Jaffe
a453.title: managing director of the Climate Policy Lab at Tufts University
a453.speech: Wrote: “West needs to help and encourage countries who are highly dependent on oil for their economics to pivot with us, go away from oil and gas”.

a453.speaker: Opinion polls (cited)
a453.name: Opinion polls (cited)
a453.speech: Have shown a continued trend of favourable opinions towards the influence Chinese presence has on African societies.

a453.speaker: International Energy Agency (IEA)
a453.name: International Energy Agency (IEA)
a453.speech: Five years ago described four large-scale technology revolutions that were supposed to change the energy equilibrium in the world, all grounded in geopolitics: discovery and exploration of shale gas and oil in the United States; the emergence of cheap photovoltaic panels; China moving to clean energy; and electricity becoming the major energy conduit, replacing oil and coal.

a460.speaker: Axel Tibinyane, acting executive director of health and social welfare policy in the Namibian Health Ministry
a460.name: Axel Tibinyane
a460.title: acting executive director of health and social welfare policy in the Namibian Health Ministry
a460.speech: Revealed that a total of 3 700 Namibians succumbed to HIV/AIDS in 2023, with 2 100 being women and 1 600 men, sharing the statistics at the 19th International Conference on HIV Treatment, Pathogenesis and Prevention Research in Resource-Limited Settings in Windhoek ; Said 400 males between the ages of 15 and 24 tested positive for HIV in 2023, while 1 700 females between the ages of 15 and 24 tested positive for HIV in the same year.

a460.speaker: Axel Tibinyane, acting executive director of health and social welfare policy in the Namibian Health Ministry
a460.name: Axel Tibinyane
a460.title: acting executive director of health and social welfare policy in the Namibian Health Ministry
a460.speech: Highlighted significant progress in the national HIV response, revealing that 93% of Namibians knew their HIV status in 2023, while 95% of those living with HIV have been on treatment ; “Of those on treatment, 98% have been virally suppressed,” he added.

a460.speaker: Victoria Kamule, executive director of Tonata People Living with HIV
a460.name: Victoria Kamule
a460.title: executive director of Tonata People Living with HIV
a460.speech: Raised concerns about the impact of reduced funding from the United States government through USAID, saying this decision has placed a significant strain on community-level HIV response and efforts, affecting crucial peer support networks and outreach programmes ; “It is important to remember that behind every funding cut is a person – a mother, a young woman, a peer educator, a father, son, a person who used drugs, and their lives are put at risk,” Kamule emphasised.

a460.speaker: Elijah Ngurare, Namibian Prime Minister (statement delivered on his behalf)
a460.name: Elijah Ngurare
a460.title: Namibian Prime Minister (statement delivered on his behalf)
a460.speech: Said Namibia has made significant progress towards achieving the UNAIDS 95-95-95 fast-track targets, which aim to end the AIDS epidemic by 2030 by achieving specific milestones in HIV testing, treatment and viral suppression; Namibia was recognised by the World Health Organisation last year for its progress in eliminating the mother-to-child transmission of HIV and the hepatitis B virus, he added.

a505.speaker: Somalia's Ministry of Interior, Federal Affairs and Reconciliation
a505.name: Somalia's Ministry of Interior
a505.title: Federal Affairs and Reconciliation
a505.speech: Announced the rollout of a Unified Digital Civil Registration Service, now operational in 19 districts across the Federal Member States of Jubbaland, South West, Hirshabelle, Galmudug, and Northeastern State.

a505.speaker: Officials (Somali government, unnamed)
a505.name: Officials (Somali government
a505.title: unnamed)
a505.speech: Officials say this will help overcome longstanding challenges in obtaining official documentation and improve service delivery.

a505.speaker: Government of Somalia
a505.name: Government of Somalia
a505.speech: Somalia reaffirmed its commitment to the continental call for advancing Civil Registration and Vital Statistics systems so that every African citizen is counted and included in official government records.

a549.speaker: Government of the Republic of Benin (Decree No. 2009-542 of 20 October 2009)
a549.name: Government of the Republic of Benin (Decree No. 2009-542 of 20 October 2009)
a549.speech: The decree creates the One-Stop Shop for Business Formalisation (GUFE) as a public administrative body with legal personality and organisational and financial autonomy under the supervision of the Ministry in charge of Trade, confers increased powers and resources on GUFE compared with the CFE, and reduces the number of formalities required for the creation, modification, cessation of activity and dissolution of businesses.

a549.speaker: Geca-Prospective consultancy
a549.name: Geca-Prospective consultancy
a549.speech: Gave a comparative presentation on the innovations contained in the new decree on the One-Stop Shop for Business Formalisation compared with the former decree that created the Business Formalities Centre.

a587.speaker: The widow, children, grandchildren and allied families of Dr Effi Yamien (death/thanksgiving notice)
a587.name: The widow
a587.title: children, grandchildren and allied families of Dr Effi Yamien (death/thanksgiving notice)
a587.speech: Deeply touched by the many marks of compassion and support shown at the time of the death of their beloved brother, brother-in-law, uncle, friend, colleague, father, father-in-law, grandfather and husband, Dr Effi Yamien, and unable to reach each of you individually, express their profound gratitude and their most sincere thanks to Minister Kandia Camara, Adama Coulibaly, Ida Camara, and Senator Boby Assa Eminiene, with particular thanks to the various Pastors, to the king of Moronou, to the traditional and cantonal chiefs and to the order of pharmacists of Côte d'Ivoire. "A year already, wow! How time flies... Your smile, your calm and your voice, although engraved in us, are terribly missed!"

a595.speaker: Ukraine (Ukrainian side)
a595.name: Ukraine (Ukrainian side)
a595.speech: Said talks with the United States in Saudi Arabia began "very constructively" on Tuesday, with a partial ceasefire with Russia on the table.

a595.speaker: Andriy Yermak, Ukrainian presidency chief of staff
a595.name: Andriy Yermak
a595.title: Ukrainian presidency chief of staff
a595.speech: "We are ready to do everything to achieve peace," told reporters as he entered Tuesday's meeting ; "The meeting with the US team started very constructively; we continue our work," Yermak said on social media Tuesday.

a595.speaker: Kyiv officials
a595.name: Kyiv officials
a595.speech: Said the "largest drone attack in history", in which hundreds of drones slammed into Moscow and other areas overnight, was intended to push Russian President Vladimir Putin to agree to the aerial and naval ceasefire.

a595.speaker: Andriy Kovalenko, national security council official responsible for countering disinformation
a595.name: Andriy Kovalenko
a595.title: national security council official responsible for countering disinformation
a595.speech: "This is an additional signal to Putin that he should also be interested in a ceasefire in the air."

a595.speaker: Russia's army
a595.name: Russia's army
a595.speech: Said it intercepted 337 drones around the country.

a595.speaker: Volodymyr Zelensky, Ukrainian President
a595.name: Volodymyr Zelensky
a595.title: Ukrainian President
a595.speech: Has said he is still willing to sign the agreement pushed by Trump that would give the United States control over Ukrainian mineral resources.

a595.speaker: Marco Rubio, US Secretary of State
a595.name: Marco Rubio
a595.title: US Secretary of State
a595.speech: Said the minerals deal would not be the focus of Tuesday's meeting.

a595.speaker: Marco Rubio, US Secretary of State
a595.name: Marco Rubio
a595.title: US Secretary of State
a595.speech: Said the aid suspension was "something I hope we can resolve" in the talks; said the United States had not cut off intelligence for defensive operations.

a595.speaker: Marco Rubio, US Secretary of State
a595.name: Marco Rubio
a595.title: US Secretary of State
a595.speech: Signalled that the Trump administration would likely be pleased by such a proposal: "I'm not saying that alone is enough, but it's the kind of concession you would need to see in order to end the conflict," he told reporters ; "You're not going to get a ceasefire and an end to this war unless both sides make concessions." ; Said he did not expect to be "drawing lines on a map" towards a final deal in the Jeddah meeting, but said he would bring ideas back to Russia.

a595.speaker: Marco Rubio, US Secretary of State
a595.name: Marco Rubio
a595.title: US Secretary of State
a595.speech: Said on Monday that the United States would also object to "antagonistic" language on Russia at an upcoming gathering of Group of Seven foreign ministers.

a595.speaker: Dmitri Peskov, Kremlin spokesperson
a595.name: Dmitri Peskov
a595.title: Kremlin spokesperson
a595.speech: Asked whether the overnight drone attack could derail peace talks, said: "There are no (peace) negotiations yet, so there is nothing to disrupt here." ; He also declined earlier to comment on Russia's stance on the proposed partial ceasefire: "It is absolutely impossible to talk about positions yet," he said ; "The Americans will find out only today, as they themselves say, from Ukraine to what extent Ukraine is ready for peace."

a595.speaker: Russia (Russian government)
a595.name: Russia (Russian government)
a595.speech: Said it had retaken 12 settlements in its Kursk region that Ukraine had captured in a bid for bargaining leverage.

a595.speaker: Ukrainian official (anonymous)
a595.name: Ukrainian official (anonymous)
a595.speech: Told AFP on Monday that Ukraine will lay out its support for a limited ceasefire in the sky and at sea.

a595.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a595.name: Donald Trump
a595.title: US President
a595.speech: Last week also threatened further sanctions against Russia to force it to the table as it carried out strikes on Ukraine; suggested Ukraine was to blame for the war.

a869.speaker: Budget 25 strategy (Botswana government document)
a869.name: Budget 25 strategy (Botswana government document)
a869.speech: Published last week, outlined the direction for the economy; growing sources of revenue beyond minerals was seen as a crucial part of forging a sustainable fiscal pathway.

a869.speaker: Boko Duma, President of Botswana
a869.name: Boko Duma
a869.title: President of Botswana
a869.speech: “By introducing hemp-based industries, we will create an entirely new economic sector, previously unknown to our republic.”

a962.speaker: Bashar al-Assad, former President of Syria (written statement)
a962.name: Bashar al-Assad
a962.title: former President of Syria (written statement)
a962.speech: Said that as terrorism spread across Syria and reached Damascus on the evening of Saturday 7 December 2024, questions arose about his fate amid “a torrent of disinformation and distorted narratives, which tried to present international terrorism as a liberation revolution for Syria”; stated that his departure from the country “was neither premeditated nor did it take place in the final hours of the fighting, contrary to what has been falsely claimed,” and that he remained in Damascus carrying out his responsibilities until the early hours of Sunday 8 December 2024, then travelled to Latakia in coordination with Russian allies to supervise military operations; said that upon arriving at the Hmeimim air base it became clear that Syrian forces had completely withdrawn from the battle lines and the army’s last positions had fallen, and that with intensifying drone attacks on the Russian base it became impossible to leave, after which Moscow asked the base command to organise an immediate evacuation to Russia on the evening of Sunday 8 December.

a962.speaker: Bashar al-Assad, former President of Syria (written statement)
a962.name: Bashar al-Assad
a962.title: former President of Syria (written statement)
a962.speech: Said that during these events “the idea of asylum or resignation was never considered, neither by me nor by any individual or entity,” and that the only course of action was to continue resisting the terrorist assault; reaffirmed that the person who from the first day of the war refused to trade his nation’s salvation for his personal safety is the same person who stood alongside officers and soldiers on the front lines and did not leave his post during fourteen years of war; said that one who never abandoned the Palestinian and Lebanese resistance nor betrayed his allies could not abandon his own people or betray the army and nation; stated that he never sought office for personal gain but regarded himself as “the guardian of a national project” drawing strength from the faith of the Syrian people; said that when the State falls into the hands of terrorism and the capacity to make a meaningful contribution disappears, any office becomes meaningless, while affirming his unshakeable sense of belonging to Syria and his hope that Syria will rise again, free and independent.

a1588.speaker: 2022 population and housing census (Tanzania)
a1588.name: 2022 population and housing census (Tanzania)
a1588.speech: According to the 2022 population and housing census, Tanzania has a large number of young people and adolescents, totalling 21.3 million aged between 15 and 35.

a1588.speaker: Stakeholders (wadau)
a1588.name: Stakeholders (wadau)
a1588.speech: say that an increase should be expected in new HIV infections, sexually transmitted diseases, teenage pregnancies and maternal deaths as a result of the absence of the aid.

a1588.speaker: Hadija Maganga, youth leader and peer educator
a1588.name: Hadija Maganga
a1588.title: youth leader and peer educator
a1588.speech: said that access to reproductive health services and commodities for young people and young women in the country is important for the wellbeing of society, especially in this period of changes in foreign aid policies; she said adolescent girls are greatly affected by the lack of information, especially information concerning reproductive health ; "At this time when we hear reports that aid is going to end, as stakeholders we are left asking ourselves, what will the situation be? When you talk to adolescents they show clearly that there is secrecy within families; parents do not talk to them openly about reproductive health matters. Many look for information on their own; peer educators helped a great deal, and we are not sure whether the government will be able to do what USAID did" ; added that the government should find solutions for reproductive health, especially for adolescents: "The government cannot place the same emphasis as the SHARP projects do on ensuring that young people are involved."

a1588.speaker: Denis Bwana, national reproductive health expert
a1588.name: Denis Bwana
a1588.title: national reproductive health expert
a1588.speech: said the availability of these services is the right answer to tackling teenage pregnancies in the regions with high numbers, including Manyara and Morogoro, especially access to family planning services ; "Reproductive health services include matters of family planning, condom use and such medical supplies; they contribute greatly to tackling the challenges of teenage pregnancies" ; said teenage pregnancies are directly related to child marriage, because reproductive health services include accurate information reaching girls, which helps them make their own decisions; according to him such information contributes greatly to lowering HIV infections because reproductive services go together with family planning, including condom use.

a1588.speaker: Denis Bwana, national reproductive health expert
a1588.name: Denis Bwana
a1588.title: national reproductive health expert
a1588.speech: "Within it there was various health advocacy; there were community-level service providers who would go around giving education to peer groups, through programmes that were under USAID funding, who were helping to tackle these challenges. With these projects stopping, these young people cannot get much information. The remaining programmes are not enough, and even when USAID's existed they were still not sufficient — the interpretation is that young people will be at risk of infection, teenage pregnancies will increase, and child marriages [too]" ; said many teenage pregnancies contribute to maternal and newborn deaths, because the child is born to a mother who is not ready economically, biologically, psychologically and mentally; said the harm that will occur now could affect future generations.

a1588.speaker: Denis Bwana, national reproductive health expert
a1588.name: Denis Bwana
a1588.title: national reproductive health expert
a1588.speech: says the country needs to assess how it used the aid through USAID, how many experts were produced and what they can now do for the country, and that there must be accountability ; "In order to restore these services, we must relax the conditions so that there is a friendly environment — taxes; if our policies are not friendly people will quit. We must review our policies anew so that the private sector can invest in health" ; emphasised that it is important to be innovative in investing in the health sector.

a1588.speaker: Reverend Modest Pesha, Coordinator of the Christian Council of Tanzania (CCT)
a1588.name: Reverend Modest Pesha
a1588.title: Coordinator of the Christian Council of Tanzania (CCT)
a1588.speech: said it is still early to assess the effects on youth groups within the short period since the change in foreign aid policies; said access to reproductive health services and commodities for those groups is important in targeting HIV infections, teenage pregnancies, unintended pregnancies and forced marriages resulting from teenage pregnancies; also said they would help reduce maternal and child deaths, especially for those who give birth at a young age, in order to reach the SDG targets, as well as conflicts within households and the community and the breakdown of families ; "Reproductive health services include the provision of education starting at the family level, with parents breaking the silence, together with religious institutions incorporating reproductive health education into their teachings" ; emphasised that the availability of commodities should observe ethics, principles and faith teachings, age and correct use in order to avoid further harm.

a1588.speaker: Stakeholders (wadau)
a1588.name: Stakeholders (wadau)
a1588.speech: called on the government to ensure it fulfils various agreements including the Abuja Declaration, which requires countries to allocate 15 percent of their budget to health ; "We have done a good thing in maternal and child services, but if we depend more on aid our health systems will get stuck. Because we have not invested in health, all the foreign aid from the United States is little money, but look at its effect on us. This is where we should see the importance of our taxes: the first investment should be in health, second education and infrastructure. Reproductive health has been shaken more now. We must have health systems that are sustainable."

a1588.speaker: Dr Grace Magembe, Chief Medical Officer of the Government of Tanzania
a1588.name: Dr Grace Magembe
a1588.title: Chief Medical Officer of the Government of Tanzania
a1588.speech: said the matter is being handled by a team in the Prime Minister's Office which is looking at all those services, and that a report will be issued after the analysis; said no service has stopped, they are continuing, having been integrated together, and ARVs and other medicines are being obtained; however said the civil society organisations that were providing education to young people about teenage pregnancies and reproductive health are stopping ; "We are looking at how they must continue. At present community-level service providers are there, they are paid by the government and they provide all integrated services starting with public education, tuberculosis services, malaria, family planning, teenage pregnancies. We have created an integrated plan; the community-level service provider has been empowered with special training; it is among the strategies that will give us sustainability of those services, and they also provide education. This is being worked on by a team within the government, not the Ministry of Health alone" ; emphasised that all essential services, especially those concerning treatment and cure, are continuing as usual.

a1668.speaker: Umodzi Party (statement signed by Party President Hon. Thomas Wezzie Kaumba)
a1668.name: Umodzi Party (statement signed by Party President Hon. Thomas Wezzie Kaumba)
a1668.speech: Reaffirmed its support for President Lazarus Chakwera's leadership while addressing a series of critical national issues, including the suspension of the IMF loan facility, rising political violence, and the introduction of digital voting technology ahead of the September tripartite elections.

a1668.speaker: Thomas Wezzie Kaumba, Umodzi Party President
a1668.name: Thomas Wezzie Kaumba
a1668.title: Umodzi Party President
a1668.speech: Praised the government's decision to pause the Extended Credit Facility (ECF) arrangement with the International Monetary Fund, describing it as a "bold and positive" step toward economic independence. "For decades, Malawi's economy has relied heavily on foreign aid and loans. This decision marks a turning point towards building a truly self-reliant economy," Kaumba stated, noting that the country's public debt—now over K12 trillion—has placed immense pressure on citizens.

a1668.speaker: Thomas Wezzie Kaumba, Umodzi Party President
a1668.name: Thomas Wezzie Kaumba
a1668.title: Umodzi Party President
a1668.speech: Strongly condemned recent incidents of political violence in the lead-up to the elections, urging the Malawi Police Service to investigate and prosecute all perpetrators. "Political violence has no place in modern Malawi. We call on all 23 registered political parties to sign a peace accord to demonstrate their commitment to unity."

a1668.speaker: Thomas Wezzie Kaumba, Umodzi Party President
a1668.name: Thomas Wezzie Kaumba
a1668.title: Umodzi Party President
a1668.speech: Threw the party's full support behind the use of Smartmatic electronic voting technology in the upcoming elections, emphasizing that digital innovation is vital for enhancing transparency and aligning Malawi's electoral process with global democratic standards. Criticizing opposition parties that have raised concerns about the new system, Kaumba said, "We are not surprised that those who manipulated the 2019 elections with duplicate votes and correction fluid are now opposing Smartmatic. This technology ensures a credible vote, and we urge the Malawi Electoral Commission to remain resolute."

a1668.speaker: Thomas Wezzie Kaumba, Umodzi Party President
a1668.name: Thomas Wezzie Kaumba
a1668.title: Umodzi Party President
a1668.speech: Confirmed the party will not field a presidential candidate in the 2025 elections and will instead support President Chakwera and the Malawi Congress Party, citing ongoing development under the current administration. He highlighted improvements in infrastructure, social support programmes, increased student loan access, and electricity reliability as key achievements since the Tonse Alliance took office. "This government is delivering development without discrimination. Supporting President Chakwera is the only logical choice for those who love Malawi," he said. He dismissed speculation about a possible alliance with the UTM, describing the party as "an amateur" lacking national focus. He called on Malawians to remain united and hopeful, describing President Chakwera as "the Joshua" who will lead the nation to prosperity: "Let us not take five steps backwards. The Canaan we seek is within reach. Malawi needs unity. Malawi needs Umodzi."

a1702.speaker: Jeune Afrique (newspaper)
a1702.name: Jeune Afrique (newspaper)
a1702.speech: Reports two deadly jihadist attacks that occurred at the end of last week in the Eastern region of Burkina Faso, which left at least a dozen dead, both among the security forces and civilians.

a1702.speaker: Burkinabè security source (anonymous), speaking to AFP
a1702.name: Burkinabè security source (anonymous)
a1702.title: speaking to AFP
a1702.speech: "On 14 March, hundreds of terrorists attacked the detachment of the grouping of mobile intervention units (Gumi, police) based at Yamba," a locality situated about 30 kilometres from Fada N'Gourma, capital of the Eastern region.

a1702.speaker: Armed Conflict Location & Event Data (ACLED) NGO, cited by Le Monde Afrique
a1702.name: Armed Conflict Location & Event Data (ACLED) NGO
a1702.title: cited by Le Monde Afrique
a1702.speech: According to ACLED, the violence by jihadist armed groups in Burkina Faso since 2015 has caused more than 26,000 deaths, civilian and military, including more than 13,500 since the coup d'état of September 2022.

a1702.speaker: Le Monde Afrique (newspaper)
a1702.name: Le Monde Afrique (newspaper)
a1702.speech: Reports the discovery of "the oldest human presence in a tropical forest", attested in Abidjan, Côte d'Ivoire.

a1702.speaker: Study published in the journal Nature
a1702.name: Study published in the journal Nature
a1702.speech: Reveals that traces of Homo sapiens dating back 150,000 years were found in the Anyama district; before this discovery, the oldest traces of our species in this type of environment were located in Asia and Oceania, dating back 70,000 years.

a1702.speaker: Abidjan.net (Ivorian news website)
a1702.name: Abidjan.net (Ivorian news website)
a1702.speech: Announces the opening of the electoral dispute process in Côte d'Ivoire with the publication of the provisional electoral roll ahead of the October 2025 presidential election; specifies that the name of Tidjane Thiam, president of the Democratic Party of Côte d'Ivoire (PDCI-RDA), appears on the list, but that several opposition leaders, including Laurent Gbagbo and Charles Blé Goudé, are absent from it.

a1702.speaker: Le Monde Afrique (newspaper)
a1702.name: Le Monde Afrique (newspaper)
a1702.speech: Examines the impact of the freeze on development aid decided by former president Donald Trump last January in Guinea-Bissau: the country, like others in Africa, is beginning to feel the disastrous effects of this decision; in a few weeks 92% of funding was cut and the United States Agency for International Development (USAID) was dismantled, which risks seriously affecting health programmes, particularly those intended for women.

a1702.speaker: Sud Quotidien (Senegalese daily)
a1702.name: Sud Quotidien (Senegalese daily)
a1702.speech: Publishes an analysis under the title "chronicle of a slow death", describing the challenges facing traditional political formations such as the Socialist Party (PS) and the Senegalese Democratic Party (PDS) in the face of the recomposition of the post-presidential political landscape; the newspaper considers that these historic parties must redouble their ingenuity to maintain their influence in a context of a crisis of representativeness and the rise of citizen movements and social networks.

a1702.speaker: Walf Quotidien (Senegalese daily)
a1702.name: Walf Quotidien (Senegalese daily)
a1702.speech: Examines the "yo-yo game of Macky Sall" in the management of the Alliance for the Republic (APR), the former presidential party; the newspaper analyses his decision to relieve Amadou Mame Diop, former president of the National Assembly, of the coordination of the APR and replace him with Me Sidiki Kaba, his former Minister of Justice, as a manoeuvre aimed at preparing his return to the political scene.

a1728.speaker: World Food Programme (WFP) report 'The State of School Feeding Worldwide'
a1728.name: World Food Programme (WFP) report 'The State of School Feeding Worldwide'
a1728.speech: Reports that nearly 80 million additional children now benefit from school meals under government programmes, an increase of 20% compared with 2020, bringing the global total to at least 466 million children: "Progress is being made where it is most needed, with low-income countries increasing by 60% the number of children receiving school meals in just the past two years. Africa is leading this progress, with 20 million additional African children now fed through national school meal programmes" ; states that this rare development success is being led by governments around the world, motivated by solid evidence that national school meal programmes not only promote children's well-being but also have considerable benefits for smallholder farmers and local employment, while encouraging planet-friendly diets and reducing carbon emissions ; reports that global financing for school meals has more than doubled, from 43 billion US dollars in 2020 to 84 billion in 2024, with 99% now coming from national budgets, so that school meals are no longer seen as a foreign aid programme but as an effective public policy capable of driving national development, though national financing is weaker in low-income countries ; shows that school meals improve learning capacities and cognitive skills and boost results in mathematics and reading, often more effectively than teacher training or introducing technology ; underlines that school feeding programmes constitute the world's largest social safety net, generate between 7 and 35 dollars in economic benefits for every dollar invested, and generate around 7.4 million catering jobs worldwide ; reports that WFP is drawing on its operational expertise as a frontline emergency responder, as in Haiti, to help governments strengthen national systems, and that in Armenia, Benin and Iraq WFP has supported the transition of school meal programmes to full national ownership.

a1728.speaker: Cindy McCain, Executive Director of the World Food Programme (WFP)
a1728.name: Cindy McCain
a1728.title: Executive Director of the World Food Programme (WFP)
a1728.speech: "School meals are far more than just a plate of nutritious food, as important as that is. For the vulnerable children who benefit from them, they are a way out of poverty and into a new world of learning and opportunity" ; "Governments around the world, particularly in low- and middle-income countries, are showing real leadership by prioritising school meal programmes. These programmes have proven to be one of the smartest and most cost-effective investments for improving the health, education and economic prosperity of future generations over the long term. WFP is grateful for the transformative partnerships built through the School Meals Coalition, and encourages even more governments to join this global movement."

a1750.speaker: MCC World Cricket Committee (WCC)
a1750.name: MCC World Cricket Committee (WCC)
a1750.speech: Urged cricket chiefs to intervene urgently to ensure the international game can thrive alongside booming franchise competitions; acknowledged the increased playing opportunities and financial health of the game but said it was vital to make it sustainable in the long term.

a1750.speaker: MCC World Cricket Committee (WCC) (statement)
a1750.name: MCC World Cricket Committee (WCC) (statement)
a1750.speech: A statement issued by the body said the men's cricket schedule in 2023 was "saturated" with franchise competitions, which competed and overlapped with international series. "Of the domestic tournaments, only the Indian Premier League (Twenty20 competition) commands anything like a window to avoid international clashes." ; "Continued overlap and congestion will see an increasing number of players forced to choose between club and country, which will threaten the 'best v best' status that is so critical to the success and appeal of international cricket."

a1750.speaker: MCC World Cricket Committee (WCC)
a1750.name: MCC World Cricket Committee (WCC)
a1750.speech: Said the issue of overlap in the women's game between international cricket and domestic leagues was not currently a problem but urged boards to find the "optimal balance" between the two.

a1750.speaker: Ben Stokes, England Test captain
a1750.name: Ben Stokes
a1750.title: England Test captain
a1750.speech: Cited an "unsustainable" schedule when he announced last year that he was retiring from the 50-over format.

a1750.speaker: Trent Boult, New Zealand bowler
a1750.name: Trent Boult
a1750.title: New Zealand bowler
a1750.speech: Asked to be released from his contract with the Black Caps to spend more time with his family and make more room in his schedule for franchise cricket.

a1750.speaker: Sourav Ganguly, former India captain and WCC member
a1750.name: Sourav Ganguly
a1750.title: former India captain and WCC member
a1750.speech: Said Test cricket remained the "biggest platform". "That should always continue to be the pinnacle and I am sure that countries will give importance to it and find the right balance between franchise cricket and Test cricket."

a1750.speaker: Justin Langer, WCC member, former Australia opener and coach
a1750.name: Justin Langer
a1750.title: WCC member, former Australia opener and coach
a1750.speech: "The difference between international cricket and domestic T20 cricket is that the whole nation cares when their country is involved. The best players' statistics are measured at international level."

a1812.speaker: Marco Rubio, US Secretary of State
a1812.name: Marco Rubio
a1812.title: US Secretary of State
a1812.speech: Announced the visa measure on Saturday. He said it was a response to South Sudan's refusal to accept the return of its citizens being removed from the US. In his statement, Rubio said that the US would also block any arriving citizens of South Sudan at US ports of entry. He blamed "the failure of South Sudan's transitional government to accept the return of its repatriated citizens in a timely manner" ; "We will be prepared to review these actions when South Sudan is in full cooperation."

a1812.speaker: South Sudan's foreign ministry (statement)
a1812.name: South Sudan's foreign ministry (statement)
a1812.speech: Said the move was based on a case involving someone who had been incorrectly identified as South Sudanese. It added that the individual was "returned to the sending country for further processing" ; In a statement on Monday said it "deeply regrets" the blanket measure against all of the country's citizens based on "an isolated incident involving misrepresentation by an individual who is not a South Sudanese national". It said the man at the centre of the visa row was a Congolese national and he was returned to the US. It added that all supporting evidence was shared with American officials.

a1812.speaker: Christopher Landau, US Deputy Secretary of State
a1812.name: Christopher Landau
a1812.title: US Deputy Secretary of State
a1812.speech: Dismissed South Sudan's explanation as "legally irrelevant", saying the African country's embassy in Washington "certified this particular individual as one of their nationals" ; "It is unacceptable and irresponsible for South Sudanese government officials to second guess the determination of their own embassy."

a1812.speaker: Michael Makuei Lueth, South Sudan's Information Minister
a1812.name: Michael Makuei Lueth
a1812.title: South Sudan's Information Minister
a1812.speech: Told the AP news agency that the US was "attempting to find faults with the tense situation" in the country because no sovereign nation would accept foreign deportees.

a1812.speaker: Salva Kiir, President of South Sudan
a1812.name: Salva Kiir
a1812.title: President of South Sudan
a1812.speech: Accused First Vice-President Riek Machar of stirring up a new revolt.

a1982.speaker: Office of South African President Cyril Ramaphosa
a1982.name: Office of South African President Cyril Ramaphosa
a1982.speech: Said ahead of his meeting with Trump: "The visit will focus specifically on reframing bilateral, economic and commercial relations."

a1982.speaker: Cyril Ramaphosa, South African President
a1982.name: Cyril Ramaphosa
a1982.title: South African President
a1982.speech: Said on South African state television before flying to Washington: "Whether we like it or not, we are joined at the hip and we need to be talking to them."

a1982.speaker: Spokesperson for the South African trade ministry
a1982.name: Spokesperson for the South African trade ministry
a1982.speech: Said Ramaphosa will offer Trump a broad trade deal, declining to give details.

a1982.speaker: Ramaphosa's spokesperson
a1982.name: Ramaphosa's spokesperson
a1982.speech: Said discussions could include favourable tariffs for Tesla's imports into South Africa in return for building electric vehicle charging stations, and licensing for Starlink.

a1982.speaker: White House official (anonymous)
a1982.name: White House official (anonymous)
a1982.speech: Said Trump is likely to tell Ramaphosa that all U.S. companies should be exempt from "racial requirements."

a1982.speaker: John Steenhuisen, South African Agriculture Minister
a1982.name: John Steenhuisen
a1982.title: South African Agriculture Minister
a1982.speech: Said he would work to secure South African farmers' duty-free access to the U.S. market under the African Growth and Opportunity Act, which is at risk from Trump's tariff regime.

a1982.speaker: Donald Trump, U.S. President (February 7 executive order)
a1982.name: Donald Trump
a1982.title: U.S. President (February 7 executive order)
a1982.speech: Cited the country's land reform law and "hateful rhetoric and government actions" it said were fuelling disproportionate violence against white landowners.

a1982.speaker: Pretoria (South African government)
a1982.name: Pretoria (South African government)
a1982.speech: Said "the foundational premise of this order lacks factual accuracy and fails to recognise South Africa's profound and painful history of colonialism and apartheid" ; says the racial discrimination claims on which Trump offered refuge to white minority Afrikaners are unfounded.

a1982.speaker: Elon Musk, Trump's billionaire ally
a1982.name: Elon Musk
a1982.title: Trump's billionaire ally
a1982.speech: Has accused Ramaphosa of pursuing anti-white policies, which Ramaphosa rejects.

a1982.speaker: Crime statistics
a1982.name: Crime statistics
a1982.speech: Show no evidence that white people are disproportionately targeted.

a1982.speaker: F.W. de Klerk, last white president of South Africa
a1982.name: F.W. de Klerk
a1982.title: last white president of South Africa
a1982.speech: Spoke of Ramaphosa's "silver tongue and honeyed phrases."

a1982.speaker: Jan Venter, lecturer in politics and international relations at South Africa's North-West University
a1982.name: Jan Venter
a1982.title: lecturer in politics and international relations at South Africa's North-West University
a1982.speech: "He is an international businessman, and I think that he must put that side of his personality first."

a1982.speaker: Joshua Meservey, senior fellow at conservative U.S. think tank the Hudson Institute
a1982.name: Joshua Meservey
a1982.title: senior fellow at conservative U.S. think tank the Hudson Institute
a1982.speech: Said critical minerals were likely to be discussed as they were a priority for Trump, but cautioned that deal-making may not be sufficient to mend ties: "There's political problems here that lie at the heart of the breakdown in the relationship."

a2090.speaker: Government of Cabo Verde (press release sent to Inforpress)
a2090.name: Government of Cabo Verde (press release sent to Inforpress)
a2090.speech: Stated that the MCC Regional Compact will deepen cooperation between Cabo Verde and the United States, contributing to the diversification of the Cabo Verdean economy, to accelerating the potential for economic growth and to building shared prosperity, namely through the development of connectivity and the digital economy.

a2090.speaker: Government of Cabo Verde (press release/note)
a2090.name: Government of Cabo Verde (press release/note)
a2090.speech: "We successfully implemented the First and Second MCC Compacts and the experience of that journey will be duly capitalised upon. The Government of Cabo Verde has guaranteed the full involvement of the MCC in decisions and will continue to do so at all stages of the programme's assembly and, in this way, ensures an efficient decision-making process, accelerating the processes, guaranteeing concerted choices and thus mitigating the risks of failure."

a2090.speaker: Government of Cabo Verde (press release/communique)
a2090.name: Government of Cabo Verde (press release/communique)
a2090.speech: The communique states that in assembling the investment programme and implementing the Regional Compact, partner coordination mechanisms will be valued and projects should be included that guarantee the harmonisation of contributions from other donors, the private sector and other stakeholders; that efficient inter-ministerial mechanisms, inter-sectoral alignment and coordinated action will be guaranteed; that the Government has already designated and validated with the MCC a national technical team approved by the Council of Ministers which "provides the necessary guarantees" for the next 24 months of negotiation with the MCC; and that current appointments are aligned with MCC regulations, which has guaranteed the necessary financing for the national team, including the payment of salaries.

a2290.speaker: Dambisa Moyo, author of Dead Aid
a2290.name: Dambisa Moyo
a2290.title: author of Dead Aid
a2290.speech: In Dead Aid, Dambisa Moyo discusses why aid does not really work in most African countries that are dependent on the West for survival. She views the aid that comes to these countries as harmful because it perpetuates corruption and dependency, rather than promoting sustainable development and economic growth. ; For more than 50 years, we have been receiving aid from the West, which, as Moyo observes, has not significantly developed us.

a2290.speaker: Donald Trump, United States President
a2290.name: Donald Trump
a2290.title: United States President
a2290.speech: Moyo's sentiments were recently echoed by United States (US) President Donald Trump, who, among other things, has frozen aid provided to us through the US Agency for International Development (USaid); his threat to completely shut down USaid would be a disaster for the developing world.

a2290.speaker: Government of Malawi
a2290.name: Government of Malawi
a2290.speech: has said that it is looking for alternatives to USaid.

a2461.speaker: Blantyre City Council (statement signed by chief executive officer Dennis Chinseu)
a2461.name: Blantyre City Council (statement signed by chief executive officer Dennis Chinseu)
a2461.speech: BCC has announced an upward adjustment of property values effective April 1, 2025. A statement signed by the council's chief executive officer Dennis Chinseu indicates that residential property levies have been revised by 0.00127 (which means 10 percent) of the total value of the property while for commercial property, the rate has been revised to 0.00324 (about 35 percent).

a2461.speaker: Abbas Panjwani, representing the business community
a2461.name: Abbas Panjwani
a2461.title: representing the business community
a2461.speech: Said the hike would punish innocent people: "At a time when businesses are already grappling with rising operational costs, inflationary pressures and economic uncertainty, a hike in property rates will only add to their financial strain. This burden will be particularly severe for small and medium-size enterprises, potentially leading to job losses, reduced investment and, in some cases, business closure— ultimately hindering the city's economic growth."

a2461.speaker: Other property owners (Blantyre)
a2461.name: Other property owners (Blantyre)
a2461.speech: Described the move as a slap in their face, saying Malawians are already struggling to afford basic necessities in the midst of an errant inflation rate.

a2461.speaker: G.M. Wawanya, property owner
a2461.name: G.M. Wawanya
a2461.title: property owner
a2461.speech: "However, property owners have already been complaining about very high city rates; that the last Quinquennial valuation exercise was not done well and that objections to the valuers so inserted were not exhausted. Instead of dealing with the queries, the council proceeds to increase the rates further, thereby contributing to the rise of the cost of living in the city. All this is being done when there are complaints of poor service delivery and the general state of public infrastructure in the city is at its lowest standard. There is also the issue that it is the same property owners that bear the blunt of this increase. Why not increase the tax base by including areas that are outside the city boundary (peri-urban) such as Mpemba, Chileka, Ngumbe, Lunzu, etc, into the city so that they become rateable. Such a move [changing the rate in Kwacha] is insensitive and politically naive in that at a time the government is trying hard to lower inflation, an arm of the same government is doing the opposite."

a2461.speaker: Mike Mangwanya, owner of a commercial building in Blantyre
a2461.name: Mike Mangwanya
a2461.title: owner of a commercial building in Blantyre
a2461.speech: Said the adjustment was poorly timed: "We are complaining about rising commodity prices and this means that landlords and landladies will have to increase their rentals and Malawians who have no property will be at the receiving end of all this."

a2461.speaker: Dennis Chinseu, Blantyre City Council chief executive officer
a2461.name: Dennis Chinseu
a2461.title: Blantyre City Council chief executive officer
a2461.speech: Defended the move, saying they would like to expand their revenue base: "What we are doing is trying to top up our resources so that we can ably provide our services. However, we are aware of the situation on the ground and, so, we have done our best not to penalise the people. You can see that the adjustments are not that high."

a2461.speaker: Macdonald Gondwe, Mzuzu City Council publicist
a2461.name: Macdonald Gondwe
a2461.title: Mzuzu City Council publicist
a2461.speech: Said they last made the adjustment in 2014 and that the hike had been made to improve service provision in the city ; Gondwe added that they adjust the mill rate after 10 years but that it had taken them 11 years to announce the adjustment, which he described as reasonable ; "Usually, the resources that the council gets from the city rates are the same resources we use to provide essential services to the city. So, with that adjustment, we feel like we will provide the much-needed services to the people of Mzuzu because we will be able to collect enough [money]."

a2461.speaker: Ken Msonda, Association of Real Estate Agents in Malawi Area President
a2461.name: Ken Msonda
a2461.title: Association of Real Estate Agents in Malawi Area President
a2461.speech: Said the decision had been made without consulting them or other traders, which is not good considering the tough economic times that the citizenry is facing ; However, Msonda appealed to property owners to ensure that they remit the mill rates as failure to do so cripples operations of councils ; "It is something good but has been done at the wrong time. They should have given the citizenry and us an opportunity to give them our side of the story. We are really concerned that there were no consultations made."

a2461.speaker: Mzuzu City Council (announcement)
a2461.name: Mzuzu City Council (announcement)
a2461.speech: MCC has also announced that all business premise licences for the 2024-25 financial year will expire on March 31, 2025.

a2510.speaker: Civil society organisations
a2510.name: Civil society organisations
a2510.speech: Have raised concerns that diminished funding to provinces, both through the equitable share and through conditional grants, may result in crucial HIV/AIDS targets being missed.

a2510.speaker: National Treasury of South Africa
a2510.name: National Treasury of South Africa
a2510.speech: Has failed to provide clear information or concrete plans to assist provinces to meet their HIV programme targets amidst these budget constraints.

a2510.speaker: Antonio Izazola Licea, UNAIDS Special Advisor for Resources Tracking and Finances
a2510.name: Antonio Izazola Licea
a2510.title: UNAIDS Special Advisor for Resources Tracking and Finances
a2510.speech: Warned in 2017 that "with donor support plateauing and expected to decline, the success of South Africa's HIV programme will rest on its ability to mobilise and manage a sustainable flow of domestic resources."

a2510.speaker: Thembisa model (mathematical model of South Africa's HIV epidemic)
a2510.name: Thembisa model (mathematical model of South Africa's HIV epidemic)
a2510.speech: According to the latest outputs from the Thembisa model, in 2020 92.4% of people living with HIV knew their status; 71.9% of those diagnosed were on HIV treatment, and 91.2% of those on treatment were virally suppressed; the model shows that the highest incidence rates are among female sex workers and men who have sex with men, and version 4.3 estimated a PrEP coverage rate of only 3% and 1% in female sex workers and men who have sex with men, respectively.

a2510.speaker: Health activists
a2510.name: Health activists
a2510.speech: Have called for closer interrogation of the effectiveness of the HIV conditional grant.

a2510.speaker: Yogan Pillay, former Deputy Director-General in the National Department of Health
a2510.name: Yogan Pillay
a2510.title: former Deputy Director-General in the National Department of Health
a2510.speech: "These groups require special attention with respect to prevention and significantly increased access to treatment."

a2510.speaker: Cyril Ramaphosa, President of South Africa
a2510.name: Cyril Ramaphosa
a2510.title: President of South Africa
a2510.speech: In 2019 publicly launched an HIV programme for sex workers and declared that 'sex work is work'.

a2510.speaker: HIV/AIDS Life Skills conditional grant (stated strategic goals)
a2510.name: HIV/AIDS Life Skills conditional grant (stated strategic goals)
a2510.speech: Some of the strategic goals of the conditional grant include "addressing social and structural drivers of HIV" and "contribut[ing] to preventing new HIV, STIs, and TB infections."

a2510.speaker: Supplementary Budget Review (2020)
a2510.name: Supplementary Budget Review (2020)
a2510.speech: Accounting for the reduction, the Supplementary Budget Review explained that "All planned training sessions for over 20 000 educators [were] cancelled" in 2020.

a2510.speaker: Research from around the world, including South Africa
a2510.name: Research from around the world
a2510.title: including South Africa
a2510.speech: Has found that effective comprehensive sexuality education programmes delivered by well-trained teachers result in improved knowledge about HIV and pregnancy prevention; decreased sexual risk-taking; the prevention of learners having multiple concurrent sexual partners; improved attitudes towards sexual refusal and condom use and delayed sexual debut.

a2630.speaker: Bob Collymore, Safaricom CEO
a2630.name: Bob Collymore
a2630.title: Safaricom CEO
a2630.speech: Made this presentation to parliament’s committee on ICT, which is inquiring into legislative and regulatory gaps affecting competition in Kenya’s telecommunications sector.

a2630.speaker: Safaricom
a2630.name: Safaricom
a2630.speech: Believes its mission is to transform lives: through technology it enables farmers to improve how they farm and access farm inputs, enables learners to access education materials through platforms such as Shupavu 291, and enables Kenyans to access medical services even in remote areas, bridging the geographical challenge of access to medical care.

a2630.speaker: Safaricom
a2630.name: Safaricom
a2630.speech: Says that because of its growth it is “now considered a Dominant Operator that should be singled out for punishment for simply being successful,” in spite of the regulator’s assertions to the contrary; argues the Analysys Mason Report’s proposed remedies will punish Safaricom’s customers, stifle innovation, discourage investment and reward competitors who do not invest in their networks, by introducing retail price controls that raise the rates of Safaricom’s services and force customers to migrate to competitors, creating an artificial competitive landscape.

a2630.speaker: Analysys Mason Report on Telecommunication Competition Market Study
a2630.name: Analysys Mason Report on Telecommunication Competition Market Study
a2630.speech: On the basis of which the Communications Authority (CA) seeks to declare Safaricom dominant in certain market segments, it proposes a number of remedies or interventions, recommending: prohibition on individually tailored loyalty schemes and promotions; replicability of retail tariffs, requiring Safaricom to justify at least five days before launch that proposals can be replicated by a reasonably efficient operator; prohibition of on-net discounts; prohibition on surcharges for cross-platform money transfers; and national roaming for a period of five years on 2G, 3G and 4G for other Tier 1 mobile operators in counties identified for regulated tower sharing.

a2630.speaker: Communications Authority of Kenya (CA)
a2630.name: Communications Authority of Kenya (CA)
a2630.speech: Seeks to declare Safaricom dominant in certain market segments on the basis of the Analysys Mason Report.

a2630.speaker: Safaricom
a2630.name: Safaricom
a2630.speech: Says on the on-net discount remedy that it implemented this measure for the last three years and has continuously publicised its calling rates on the website, promotional materials and through the media, noting “our competitors are doing this and are not prohibited”; says cross-platform transfer parity is already happening through interoperability achieved via an operator-led process supervised by the CBK and Ministry for ICT, and that it expects to extend this to Telkom Kenya and all other mobile money service providers; and says its concern with a blanket national roaming intervention is that it rewards operators who have not invested in rolling out base stations as all Tier 1 licensees are obligated to do.

a2709.speaker: Government of Cabo Verde (post on Facebook)
a2709.name: Government of Cabo Verde (post on Facebook)
a2709.speech: Said the prime minister was in S. Miguel and met "with farmers to assess the impacts of this water mobilisation policy"; it was reported that drip irrigation has produced concrete results, guaranteeing the availability of water, and that the government co-finances 50 per cent of the cost of the materials.

a2741.speaker: Clementine Nkweta-Salami, UN Resident and Humanitarian Coordinator in Sudan
a2741.name: Clementine Nkweta-Salami
a2741.title: UN Resident and Humanitarian Coordinator in Sudan
a2741.speech: Urged major government donors to reconsider their decisions to reduce funding for life-saving programs and urged others to urgently step up to help fill the gaps left by these devastating cuts. “Sudden funding cuts by top government donors are a catastrophic blow to humanitarian assistance in Sudan, a country in the grip of one of the deadliest humanitarian crises of our times,” she said in a statement. ; “The reductions come at a time when the needs in Sudan have never been greater, with more than half of the population hungry and famine spreading.” ; Stated that for decades, humanitarian donors have been a lifeline for Sudan, and contributed $1.8 billion in 2024 through the Sudan humanitarian response plan: “This year, the needs are even greater – $4.2 billion is required to provide humanitarian aid in Sudan, yet only 6.3 per cent of the funding has been received.” ; Added that the abrupt funding cuts and suspensions will end life-saving humanitarian assistance for millions of women, children and other vulnerable groups across the country: “Without urgent funding, famine is likely to spread in the coming months. This is a time when every lifeline must flow to save lives. I call on all our major donors to reconsider their decisions to reduce funding for life-saving humanitarian assistance in Sudan.” ; “I also urge other governments, donors, foundations, charities, faith-based networks, the private sector and individuals to urgently step up to help fill the gaps left by these devastating reductions.”

a2741.speaker: The humanitarian community in Sudan
a2741.name: The humanitarian community in Sudan
a2741.speech: Said on Sunday that the country needs $2.7 billion to address the most urgent needs of 14.7 million people this year.

a2741.speaker: UN-OCHA
a2741.name: UN-OCHA
a2741.speech: Said famine has been confirmed in at least 5 areas in Sudan and is likely to expand in the next 3 months as conflict and restrictions to humanitarian access persist.

a2750.speaker: Abdisalam Abdi Ali, Somali Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation
a2750.name: Abdisalam Abdi Ali
a2750.title: Somali Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation
a2750.speech: Appreciated Azerbaijan's role in strengthening ties and emphasized the importance of developing a partnership that delivers significant and enduring benefits to both countries.

a2750.speaker: Ali Asadov, Prime Minister of Azerbaijan
a2750.name: Ali Asadov
a2750.title: Prime Minister of Azerbaijan
a2750.speech: Reaffirmed that Azerbaijan places great importance on strengthening relations with Somalia and expressed satisfaction with the mutual support the two countries continue to provide each other within international organizations.

a2759.speaker: IPC (Integrated Food Security Phase Classification) analysis/report
a2759.name: IPC (Integrated Food Security Phase Classification) analysis/report
a2759.speech: According to its latest analysis, more than half a million people in the Gaza Strip are now trapped in famine conditions, marked by generalised hunger, distress and avoidable deaths; by the end of September more than 640,000 Gazans are expected to fall into the most extreme level of food insecurity, while 1.14 million will be in an "emergency" situation and nearly 400,000 in "crisis"; the critical famine thresholds - extreme food deprivation, acute malnutrition and hunger-related deaths - have now been reached; more than 12,000 children were identified as suffering from acute malnutrition in July alone, six times more than at the start of the year; by 2026, 43,400 children could be exposed to a risk of death linked to malnutrition, along with 55,000 pregnant or breastfeeding women; already one baby in five is born premature or underweight.

a2759.speaker: Volker Turk, UN High Commissioner for Human Rights
a2759.name: Volker Turk
a2759.title: UN High Commissioner for Human Rights
a2759.speech: Declared that the use of starvation as a weapon of war constitutes a war crime; reacted gravely to the official announcement of famine in Gaza, saying the situation is "the direct result of the actions carried out by the Israeli government": "Using hunger as a method of war constitutes a war crime", adding that "the resulting deaths could also amount to the war crime of wilful killing"; urged the Israeli authorities to "take immediate measures to put an end to the famine" and to guarantee unhindered access for humanitarian aid.

a2759.speaker: Tom Fletcher, UN Under-Secretary-General for Humanitarian Affairs and Emergency Relief Coordinator (OCHA)
a2759.name: Tom Fletcher
a2759.title: UN Under-Secretary-General for Humanitarian Affairs and Emergency Relief Coordinator (OCHA)
a2759.speech: Delivered a damning assessment before journalists accredited to the UN in Geneva: "This is a famine! Famine is in Gaza!", he hammered angrily. "A predictable and preventable famine, caused by cruelty, justified by vengeance, permitted by indifference and sustained by complicity."

a2759.speaker: Tom Fletcher, UN Under-Secretary-General for Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA)
a2759.name: Tom Fletcher
a2759.title: UN Under-Secretary-General for Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA)
a2759.speech: Directly accuses Israel of blocking the delivery of aid, evoking "food stocks piling up at the borders" while families "have to choose which child to feed": "This is a famine a few hundred metres from food, in a fertile land", he insisted; according to him, "some Israeli leaders openly promote it as a weapon of war". ; Stresses that while the Israeli authorities continue to deny the existence of a famine, part of Israeli civil society, including survivors of 7 October, is now demanding the opening of the crossing points: "We know how to deliver aid at scale. We have done it elsewhere and we can do it again, but they have to let us work." ; Concluded his plea with an appeal to Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu: "Enough! Stop firing! Open the crossings, in the north as in the south! Let food and medicine in, on the massive scale required. Too many lives have already been lost, but it is not too late for the others. For humanity, let us in!"

a2759.speaker: Cindy McCain, Executive Director of the World Food Programme (WFP)
a2759.name: Cindy McCain
a2759.title: Executive Director of the World Food Programme (WFP)
a2759.speech: "The warnings have been clear for months. What we urgently need is a massive influx of aid, safer conditions and proven distribution systems to reach those who need it most."

a2759.speaker: Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, Director-General of the World Health Organization (WHO)
a2759.name: Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus
a2759.title: Director-General of the World Health Organization (WHO)
a2759.speech: Warned that the devastation is widespread: the health system is in ruins, drinking water and electricity are almost non-existent and 98% of Gaza's cultivable land is destroyed or inaccessible; minor illnesses are becoming deadly in a population weakened by hunger: "Even common infections such as diarrhoea or respiratory illnesses are now fatal for children."

a2759.speaker: Four UN agencies (FAO, UNICEF, WFP and WHO) (joint appeal)
a2759.name: Four UN agencies (FAO
a2759.title: UNICEF, WFP and WHO) (joint appeal)
a2759.speech: Launched a joint appeal for an immediate ceasefire and unhindered humanitarian access; said they are "gravely concerned" at the prospect of an increased military offensive in Gaza City and fear "even more devastating" consequences for civilians already on the brink of collapse.

a2759.speaker: Qu Dongyu, Director-General of the FAO
a2759.name: Qu Dongyu
a2759.title: Director-General of the FAO
a2759.speech: "Access to food is not a privilege, it is a fundamental right."

a2759.speaker: Catherine Russell, Executive Director of UNICEF
a2759.name: Catherine Russell
a2759.title: Executive Director of UNICEF
a2759.speech: Described "children too weak to cry or eat, babies dying of hunger and preventable diseases, parents with nothing to give".

a2759.speaker: Israeli authorities
a2759.name: Israeli authorities
a2759.speech: Continue to deny the existence of a famine.

a2779.speaker: Somali diaspora in Sweden and the United States
a2779.name: Somali diaspora in Sweden and the United States
a2779.speech: Has expressed its support for the defense and economic cooperation agreement between Somalia and Turkey, which was approved by the Somali parliament on Wednesday.

a2779.speaker: Somali community living in Sweden
a2779.name: Somali community living in Sweden
a2779.speech: Welcomed the agreement and congratulated the Somali government and President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud for taking this historic step.

a2779.speaker: Mohamed Hamdi Sheikh Ahmed, chairman of the Somali community in Sweden
a2779.name: Mohamed Hamdi Sheikh Ahmed
a2779.title: chairman of the Somali community in Sweden
a2779.speech: Said they stand by the agreement and the defense of their country's sea and land.

a2779.speaker: Somali community living in the United States, especially in Minnesota
a2779.name: Somali community living in the United States
a2779.title: especially in Minnesota
a2779.speech: Praised the agreement and the Somali leaders for their vision and courage.

a2779.speaker: A Somali woman living in Minnesota (anonymous)
a2779.name: A Somali woman living in Minnesota (anonymous)
a2779.speech: Said the agreement affects every Somali person in the world and makes them happy and proud.

a2779.speaker: Farhiya Khalif, representative of Galmudug in North America
a2779.name: Farhiya Khalif
a2779.title: representative of Galmudug in North America
a2779.speech: Expressed her happiness and appreciation for the agreement and the president's action in the field of maritime defense.

a2779.speaker: Hassan Sheikh Mohamud, President of Somalia
a2779.name: Hassan Sheikh Mohamud
a2779.title: President of Somalia
a2779.speech: Said the agreement with Turkey is not aimed against Ethiopia or any other country, but to support Somalia in defending its own country.

a2950.speaker: Mr. Egeh, Somalia's Finance Minister
a2950.name: Mr. Egeh
a2950.title: Somalia's Finance Minister
a2950.speech: Underscored the importance of capacity development assistance tailored to the specific needs of Somalia in achieving the country's debt relief goals ; pointed out that generic solutions are often not sufficient when dealing with the complex financial challenges of a nation, and emphasized the effectiveness of assistance that is designed to address the unique national circumstances and requirements of Somalia.

a2950.speaker: Mr. Egeh, Somalia's Finance Minister
a2950.name: Mr. Egeh
a2950.title: Somalia's Finance Minister
a2950.speech: Reiterated the government's commitment to continuing these efforts in collaboration with international partners like the IMF ; also highlighted the broader implications of context-specific assistance, suggesting that it could serve as a model for international aid effectiveness in other nations facing similar challenges.

a3017.speaker: Julius Daniel Mattai, Sierra Leone Minister of Mines and Mineral Resources
a3017.name: Julius Daniel Mattai
a3017.title: Sierra Leone Minister of Mines and Mineral Resources
a3017.speech: Advocated for the industrialization of Africa’s mining sector, saying industrialization would allow natural resources to be extracted and processed in ways that drive economic development while improving the lives of African citizens ; Stressed that despite Africa’s wealth in natural resources, economic development remains a challenge: “Africans are still struggling to make ends meet despite gaining independence decades ago. It’s heartbreaking to walk through mining communities and not see real benefits—no quality schools, hospitals, or infrastructure. I challenge my colleagues to show me a mining community that has truly prospered.”

a3017.speaker: Julius Daniel Mattai, Sierra Leone Minister of Mines and Mineral Resources
a3017.name: Julius Daniel Mattai
a3017.title: Sierra Leone Minister of Mines and Mineral Resources
a3017.speech: Highlighted the African Mining Vision (2009) as a guiding framework for ensuring that natural resources benefit African economies and urged African governments to take decisive action on resource management; emphasized the importance of “critical minerals” and insisted the continent must move beyond raw material exports to value-added processing: “Minerals don’t just appear from the sky. Someone must explore, mine, process, and manufacture before we can sell finished products” ; Encouraged civil society and social justice advocates to push for legal reforms that would revolutionize Africa’s natural resource sector.

a3017.speaker: Alpha Sesay, Sierra Leone’s Minister of Justice
a3017.name: Alpha Sesay
a3017.title: Sierra Leone’s Minister of Justice
a3017.speech: Stressed the need for legal reforms to address environmental challenges and their impact on human rights: “The environment is fundamental to human survival.
