Regardless of whether we’re working within government or civil society, we must invest in reforms that empower communities to use the law to advocate for their rights” ; Assured delegates that Sierra Leone is committed to justice sector reforms that address climate change and environmental governance, referencing Sierra Leone’s participation in the International Tribunal for the Law of the Sea’s advisory opinion on marine environmental damage in June 2024.

a3017.speaker: Alpha Sesay, Sierra Leone’s Minister of Justice
a3017.name: Alpha Sesay
a3017.title: Sierra Leone’s Minister of Justice
a3017.speech: Warned that climate change extends beyond rising temperatures and threatens food security, water access, and infrastructure: “We are witnessing erratic weather patterns, devastating floods, landslides, and worsening droughts. These crises displace vulnerable communities and threaten national stability” ; Highlighted Sierra Leone’s legal submissions before the International Court of Justice, arguing that climate change is a human rights issue, and pointed to UN Human Rights Council resolutions affirming that climate change jeopardizes fundamental rights such as life, water, food, health, and self-determination.

a3017.speaker: Both Sierra Leonean ministers (Mattai and Sesay)
a3017.name: Both Sierra Leonean ministers (Mattai and Sesay)
a3017.speech: Urged policymakers, activists, and legal professionals to push for meaningful reforms that align environmental sustainability with economic growth.

a3044.speaker: Israeli military sources (anonymous)
a3044.name: Israeli military sources (anonymous)
a3044.speech: confirmed to the Israeli site Walla and the newspaper Times of Israel that air and ground strikes had been carried out in Rafah, claiming it was a response to an attack on an Israeli military bulldozer tasked with destroying the Islamist organisation's tunnels ; told an Israeli television channel that two alleged Hamas militants had been killed.

a3044.speaker: Itamar Ben Gvir, Israeli National Security Minister
a3044.name: Itamar Ben Gvir
a3044.title: Israeli National Security Minister
a3044.speech: urged the prime minister, Benjamin Netanyahu, to resume the offensive against the Gaza Strip: "I ask the prime minister to order the Israel Defense Forces (IDF) to fully resume the fighting in the Gaza Strip with all its force."

a3044.speaker: Source in the armed wing of Hamas (anonymous)
a3044.name: Source in the armed wing of Hamas (anonymous)
a3044.speech: said the group had launched an operation in Rafah to eliminate the leader of the rival militia known as the 'Popular Forces', Yasser Abu Shabab, but that Israeli soldiers intervened to support Shabab, resulting in crossfire and causing the Israeli bulldozer to explode.

a3044.speaker: United States
a3044.name: United States
a3044.speech: warned on Saturday that it had "credible information" about an "imminent attack" by Hamas against Palestinian civilians, in a "clear violation" of the ceasefire.

a3044.speaker: Hamas
a3044.name: Hamas
a3044.speech: rejected the accusation this morning and blamed Israel for having armed and financed other militias which, it said, carried out "killings, kidnappings, thefts of humanitarian aid trucks and robberies against civilians" ; said its members in Gaza are, "with broad civilian and popular support", pursuing these gangs and holding them accountable "according to clear legal mechanisms, to protect citizens and preserve public and private property."

a3131.speaker: World Food Programme (WFP)
a3131.name: World Food Programme (WFP)
a3131.speech: is appealing to donors to provide early funding of $404 million for next year’s humanitarian operations in South Sudan to enable the agency to secure enough food to reduce hunger through 2025 ; In a press statement on Friday, WFP said it currently has no food supplies in South Sudan to preposition for next year’s humanitarian response and needs US$404 million to frontload assistance ; added that failure to do so will leave WFP reliant on expensive airdrops later in the year to reach isolated communities who are facing the most severe levels of hunger and depend on humanitarian food assistance ; the statement said funds received before the end of this year will enable WFP to preposition food by road in remote hunger-hit areas during the brief dry season window from December to April.

a3131.speaker: WFP-FAO Hunger Hotspots report
a3131.name: WFP-FAO Hunger Hotspots report
a3131.speech: warns that South Sudan is facing a combination of crises that continue to push the country towards new levels of severe food insecurity; it said the situation has left nine million people in urgent need of humanitarian assistance and protection, worsening the already dire living conditions across the country; the report underscored that South Sudan is facing unprecedented floods, impacting more than 1.3 million people nationwide, with Unity, Jonglei, Abyei Administrative Area, Western Bahr el Ghazal, and Lakes States being the most affected.

a3131.speaker: Shaun Hughes, WFP’s Acting Country Director for South Sudan
a3131.name: Shaun Hughes
a3131.title: WFP’s Acting Country Director for South Sudan
a3131.speech: “It can take months to turn pledged donor funds into food in the hands of hungry people in South Sudan. The country’s limited road networks are impassable for much of the year – particularly in the east and central parts of the country where food insecurity is highest” ; “Airdrops are always last resort for WFP. Every dollar spent on planes is a dollar not spent on food for hungry people. But there is a simple solution: get food to communities by road before they are cut off by heavy rain and flooding.”

a3131.speaker: World Food Programme (WFP)
a3131.name: World Food Programme (WFP)
a3131.speech: said it had to double the amount of food delivered by airdrops during the lean season of 2024 to meet hunger needs, adding US$30 million to overall operational costs reportedly because food aid did not arrive in the country in time ; said it was able to reduce airdrops by 70 per cent in 2019 when prepositioning was optimized due to generous donor contributions and the timely arrival of food ; said acute food insecurity in South Sudan – where 56 per cent of population already faces crisis (IPC3) or worse levels of hunger – is likely to worsen as the 2025 lean season approaches, typically starting in May.

a3169.speaker: NUDO youth organisation (critical statement)
a3169.name: NUDO youth organisation (critical statement)
a3169.speech: addresses itself, in a critical statement, to the Anglican bishops Colin Winter and R. Wood, who have evidently pledged their support to the Namibia National Convention and SWAPO; points the bishops to their actual role as missionaries: instead of disturbing the peace and sowing disunity among the inhabitants of South West Africa, they should act as proclaimers of God's word ; accuses the church representatives of being, under false pretences, in reality soldiers who wish to create chaos and confusion in other countries; because the bishops have strayed far from Christianity, NUDO denies them the authority to pray for South West Africa; as missionaries they should keep out of political power affairs ; states in conclusion that NUDO, as a peaceful organisation, rejects hatred and bloodshed.

a3169.speaker: R. F. Botha, South Africa's Ambassador in Washington
a3169.name: R. F. Botha
a3169.title: South Africa's Ambassador in Washington
a3169.speech: stated in an interview in the American capital that South Africa is considering leaving the United Nations if the exercise of its membership rights continues to be obstructed.

a3169.speaker: R. F. Botha, South Africa's Ambassador in Washington
a3169.name: R. F. Botha
a3169.title: South Africa's Ambassador in Washington
a3169.speech: stressed South Africa's wish for a peaceful solution of the disputes; in this South Africa is in agreement with the United States; the obstacles standing in the way of good cooperation between the countries should be removed.

a3169.speaker: African delegates to the UN General Assembly (unnamed)
a3169.name: African delegates to the UN General Assembly (unnamed)
a3169.speech: are said to have shown their displeasure that the President of the General Assembly, the Algerian foreign minister Bouteflika, took a decision which practically deprived South Africa of its membership rights.

a3169.speaker: Portuguese Foreign Ministry / official quarters in Lisbon
a3169.name: Portuguese Foreign Ministry / official quarters in Lisbon
a3169.speech: reported on Thursday evening that unknown mercenaries were using South West Africa as a base for the infiltration of Angola; the ministry had informed South Africa of this and pointed out the serious consequences that would arise from such a situation both for decolonisation in Angola and for peace in the area.

a3169.speaker: South African government (Pretoria, reply to Portugal)
a3169.name: South African government (Pretoria
a3169.title: reply to Portugal)
a3169.speech: again emphasises its policy of non-interference; consequently it will also not permit mercenaries to assemble, from an area under its control, for actions in a neighbouring country.

a3169.speaker: MPLA (statement in Luanda)
a3169.name: MPLA (statement in Luanda)
a3169.speech: claims that the organisation has retaken Fort Rocadas on the Kunene after an invasion of mercenaries.

a3169.speaker: Chief Justice F. H. Badenhorst, High Court in Windhoek (judgment)
a3169.name: Chief Justice F. H. Badenhorst
a3169.title: High Court in Windhoek (judgment)
a3169.speech: said in his judgment that the accused's statements had proved to be false and that the accusations against the police, that they had wanted to implicate Shipanga in guilt, were ridiculous; Shipanga's statements during the preliminary investigation had moreover not agreed with the results of later interrogations; the numerous pieces of evidence that incriminated him left the court no other choice than to exercise its duty and impose the death sentence; on account of the death sentence, the second charge, of attempted rape, would be dropped ; said that the accused could not expect any mitigating circumstances on account of his age; the accused had attended school up to Standard Three and had then worked for several years for whites in the town, so it could not be argued that the laws and customs of society were foreign to Shipanga.

a3169.speaker: Dr. W. H. Kuschke, forensic physician
a3169.name: Dr. W. H. Kuschke
a3169.title: forensic physician
a3169.speech: had set the accused's age at 24 to 26 years.

a3169.speaker: International Institute for Strategic Studies (statistical handbook)
a3169.name: International Institute for Strategic Studies (statistical handbook)
a3169.speech: According to the Institute, the countries in Africa are rearming more intensively than ever before; most countries south of the Sahara are strengthening their armed forces; Rhodesia's defence budget has risen from 21.7 million rand in 1972 to 71.4 million rand this year, so that the share of defence expenditure in Rhodesia's gross national product has grown from 1.7 to 2.6 percent; with regard to South Africa, expenditure for the country's defence has risen sharply; in Central Africa it is above all the Soviet Union that is substantially involved in the rearmament of Uganda and Somalia.

a3169.speaker: Anwar as-Sadat, President of Egypt
a3169.name: Anwar as-Sadat
a3169.title: President of Egypt
a3169.speech: In a television address justified Egypt's stance towards Israel and stated unequivocally that his country was determined to strive for a non-violent solution of the Middle East question.

a3169.speaker: Lieutenant General Mohamed Ali Fahmi, commander-in-chief of the Egyptian armed forces
a3169.name: Lieutenant General Mohamed Ali Fahmi
a3169.title: commander-in-chief of the Egyptian armed forces
a3169.speech: said in an interview that in the event of a renewed dispute with Israel, Egypt would have the better positions.

a3169.speaker: Al Ahram (Egyptian newspaper, leading article)
a3169.name: Al Ahram (Egyptian newspaper
a3169.title: leading article)
a3169.speech: According to the leading article, two possibilities present themselves for the Middle East: armed struggle or negotiations; the Soviet Union is not disposed towards negotiations and therefore prefers struggle.

a3408.speaker: Dr Lucien Dossou-Gbete, President of the Private Health Sector Platform of Benin
a3408.name: Dr Lucien Dossou-Gbete
a3408.title: President of the Private Health Sector Platform of Benin
a3408.speech: Said universal health coverage is the organisation of all health services in such a way as to guarantee individuals and communities access to quality health services, whether promotional, preventive, curative, adaptive or palliative: "It is in a civic spirit that Benin's private health sector comes to take its share in the reflection and to show the opportunities it offers to contribute to achieving universal health coverage in Benin by 2030," with a special mention for the Beninese government and partners, namely the NGO Benin Sante+, USAID and the WHO.

a3408.speaker: Karen de Andrade, representing the U.S. Ambassador to Benin
a3408.name: Karen de Andrade
a3408.title: representing the U.S. Ambassador to Benin
a3408.speech: Acknowledges the efforts made by the Beninese authorities and all the other stakeholders in implementing the Human Capital Strengthening Insurance programme (ARCH), an instrument for promoting universal health coverage: "The success of such a programme requires the active involvement of private sector actors. That is why I welcome the holding of this event, which gives you the opportunity to discuss the private sector's contribution to UHC, to identify the challenges and the possible solutions to be implemented to strengthen the public-private partnership for the benefit of UHC in Benin."

a3408.speaker: Mamoudou Harouna Djingarey, Acting Resident Representative of the World Health Organization in Benin
a3408.name: Mamoudou Harouna Djingarey
a3408.title: Acting Resident Representative of the World Health Organization in Benin
a3408.speech: Finds the theme of this edition, centred on the public-private partnership for universal health coverage, timely and appealing: "The challenges are enormous but I am sure that together we will meet them."

a3408.speaker: Veronique Tognifode, Minister of Social Affairs and Microfinance of Benin
a3408.name: Veronique Tognifode
a3408.title: Minister of Social Affairs and Microfinance of Benin
a3408.speech: "It is together that we can build a health system endowed with the resources it needs to achieve universal health coverage in Benin." According to her, the objective of Benin Sante 2021 is in line with the government's vision, which is progressively making health coverage possible for all segments of society with the support of the private sector.

a3408.speaker: Benjamin Hounkpatin, Minister of Health of Benin
a3408.name: Benjamin Hounkpatin
a3408.title: Minister of Health of Benin
a3408.speech: "In the dynamic of universal health coverage, the government has made health insurance compulsory as of 1 January 2022. I can assure you that the government has opted for an intelligent and continuous involvement of the private health sector in this process." He urges the platform to make the private health sector a powerful link in the promotion of UHC.

a3543.speaker: Presidential Decree No. 455 (signed 17 April 2012 by Russian President Dmitry Medvedev)
a3543.name: Presidential Decree No. 455 (signed 17 April 2012 by Russian President Dmitry Medvedev)
a3543.speech: Officially launched OTR “with the explicit aim of founding an independent public-service broadcaster,” providing for a Public Television Council to represent the public interest, with nominations drawn from Russia’s Public Chamber, and barring management from including sitting MPs or government officials.

a3543.speaker: State Media Monitor Global Dataset 2025, Media and Journalism Research Center (MJRC) — Dragomir, M. (2025)
a3543.name: State Media Monitor Global Dataset 2025
a3543.title: Media and Journalism Research Center (MJRC) — Dragomir, M. (2025)
a3543.speech: Assessed that OTR’s structure has effectively placed it under state control, since the President approves both the Supervisory Board members and the Director General; that OTR is funded via a combination of state budget allocations and public donations without publishing detailed financial statements, receiving approximately RUB 3 billion (~US$41.6 million) in 2020, around RUB 4.9 billion in 2021 and approximately RUB 5.5 billion in 2022, with no publicly available data on revenues, income or profit for 2023–2025; and that although conceived as a public-service broadcaster, OTR has seen its editorial independence curtailed, with programming largely confined to non-contentious, pro-government themes, opposition figures absent from its coverage, content often aligned with government narratives particularly regarding the Ukraine conflict, and no statutes or independent oversight mechanisms in place to assess or safeguard the channel’s editorial autonomy.

a3784.speaker: Palestinian sources
a3784.name: Palestinian sources
a3784.speech: Said the attack, in which at least 31 Palestinians were shot dead near a humanitarian aid centre in the south of the Gaza Strip, was carried out by Israel.

a3784.speaker: Medical Assistance Organization of the Gaza Strip (statement)
a3784.name: Medical Assistance Organization of the Gaza Strip (statement)
a3784.speech: Said in a communique that most of the injuries were to the upper part of the body and that the death toll could rise owing to the severity of the wounds ; said ambulances had difficulty reaching the site because of ongoing Israeli military activity.

a3784.speaker: Israel Defense Forces (statement)
a3784.name: Israel Defense Forces (statement)
a3784.speech: Stated on Sunday that they were unaware of the casualties caused by their fire inside the humanitarian aid distribution site and that the matter was under review.

a3784.speaker: United Nations Relief and Works Agency for Palestine Refugees (UNRWA)
a3784.name: United Nations Relief and Works Agency for Palestine Refugees (UNRWA)
a3784.speech: Stated that Israel must lift the siege and allow access for UN agencies to bring in aid and distribute it safely, in order to avert mass starvation, including of a million children.

a3856.speaker: Organisations and hospitals in Haiti
a3856.name: Organisations and hospitals in Haiti
a3856.speech: are warning of an imminent crisis in the treatment of HIV/AIDS patients, after the US drastically cut USAID foreign assistance.

a3856.speaker: Experts
a3856.name: Experts
a3856.speech: believe the real number [of Haitians living with HIV] is higher than the more than 150,000 recorded.

a3856.speaker: Marie Denis-Luque, founder of the NGO CHOAIDS, which cares for HIV-positive orphans in Cap-Haïtien
a3856.name: Marie Denis-Luque
a3856.title: founder of the NGO CHOAIDS, which cares for HIV-positive orphans in Cap-Haïtien
a3856.speech: says the medicines will only last until July.

a3856.speaker: People living with HIV demonstrating in Port-au-Prince
a3856.name: People living with HIV demonstrating in Port-au-Prince
a3856.speech: are calling for urgent action from the government.

a3856.speaker: Experts
a3856.name: Experts
a3856.speech: fear an increase in infections in a context already aggravated by violence and poverty.

a3973.speaker: International Organisation for Migration (IOM) (statement)
a3973.name: International Organisation for Migration (IOM) (statement)
a3973.speech: Recorded 8 938 migrant deaths in 2024 and said the real death toll is likely much higher given that many deaths go unreported or undocumented.

a3973.speaker: Julia Black, coordinator of the IOM’s Missing Migrants Project
a3973.name: Julia Black
a3973.title: coordinator of the IOM’s Missing Migrants Project
a3973.speech: “The rise of deaths is terrible in and of itself, but the fact that thousands remained unidentified each year is even more tragic”.

a3973.speaker: Ugochi Daniels, IOM deputy director general for operations
a3973.name: Ugochi Daniels
a3973.title: IOM deputy director general for operations
a3973.speech: “The increase in deaths across so many regions in the world shows why we need an international, holistic response that can prevent further tragic loss of life” ; “Behind every number is a human being, someone for whom the loss is devastating”.

a3973.speaker: International Organisation for Migration (IOM)
a3973.name: International Organisation for Migration (IOM)
a3973.speech: Announced days earlier that it was suspending many “lifesaving” programmes around the world and firing hundreds of employees due to United States aid cuts, impacting millions of vulnerable migrants and refugees worldwide; said the cuts forcing it to scale back or shutter programmes will have a severe impact on migrants.

a3981.speaker: Captain Hamad Bakari Hamad, Permanent Secretary in the Ministry of Blue Economy and Fisheries (Zanzibar)
a3981.name: Captain Hamad Bakari Hamad
a3981.title: Permanent Secretary in the Ministry of Blue Economy and Fisheries (Zanzibar)
a3981.speech: Stressed the importance of conducting scientific research on marine products to unlock their full economic potential for the benefit of Zanzibar and its people; urged research institutions to dedicate more effort and innovation toward enhancing the value of marine resources: “At a time when Zanzibar is promoting the blue economy as a means of improving people’s livelihoods, it is vital for researchers to harness their creativity and expertise to study marine products thoroughly for the benefit of all Zanzibaris” ; said ZAFIRI has a critical role in supporting the implementation of the blue economy policy and achieving the government’s vision, championed by President Dr Hussein Mwinyi, to economically empower citizens; expressed optimism that the newly acquired laboratory equipment will be well-maintained and used effectively.

a3981.speaker: Dr Zakaria Ali Khamis, Director General of the Zanzibar Fisheries and Marine Resources Research Institute (ZAFIRI)
a3981.name: Dr Zakaria Ali Khamis
a3981.title: Director General of the Zanzibar Fisheries and Marine Resources Research Institute (ZAFIRI)
a3981.speech: Said the investment in advanced lab equipment is aimed at ensuring that marine research is conducted efficiently, yielding reliable and modern results: “Research is the foundation upon which professionals apply their academic knowledge. Once the results are in, they must be translated into actions that serve the public and the nation” ; explained that the ZAFIRI laboratory has been significantly upgraded with modern equipment procured through funding from the Revolutionary Government of Zanzibar, totalling nearly 4bn/- for the 2024/2025 fiscal year, aligned with President Mwinyi’s goal of raising the institute to international standards; “Among the new laboratory equipment are a mercury analyser for detecting mercury contamination, an LC-MS/MS for testing organic toxins, an ICP-MS for heavy metal analysis and a UV-VIS spectrophotometer for nutrient and compound detection.”

a3981.speaker: Ms Fatma Mohammed Qadir, head of lab equipment operations at ZAFIRI
a3981.name: Ms Fatma Mohammed Qadir
a3981.title: head of lab equipment operations at ZAFIRI
a3981.speech: Noted that the availability of these machines will enable timely and accurate analysis of fishery samples, boosting the research capabilities of the institute.

a4014.speaker: United States government
a4014.name: United States government
a4014.speech: Announced a review of how previous foreign aid allocated to Nigeria and other nations has been spent ; highlighted that Boko Haram was officially designated a Foreign Terrorist Organization on November 14, 2013, a designation aimed at restricting the group’s financial resources, fundraising, and movement, and pledged continued collaboration with Nigeria and regional allies to enhance counterterrorism efforts and ensure that foreign aid reaches its intended beneficiaries.

a4014.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a4014.name: Donald Trump
a4014.title: US President
a4014.speech: Directed on January 20, 2025, that all foreign aid be halted for 90 days, citing concerns that such assistance may be contributing to global instability and failing to align with American interests.

a4014.speaker: Scott Perry, US Congressman (Republican, Pennsylvania)
a4014.name: Scott Perry
a4014.title: US Congressman (Republican, Pennsylvania)
a4014.speech: Alleged that USAID had inadvertently supported terrorist groups, including Boko Haram, making the claims during the inaugural session of the Subcommittee on Delivering on Government Efficiency last Thursday.

a4014.speaker: U.S. Mission to Nigeria (statement on X)
a4014.name: U.S. Mission to Nigeria (statement on X)
a4014.speech: In response to Perry’s accusations, emphasised on X that strict monitoring systems are in place to track past US assistance and ensure funds are used appropriately: “The United States condemns the violence and blatant disregard for human life perpetrated by Boko Haram and other terrorist groups in Nigeria and the region.”

a4207.speaker: Ghana Export Promotion Authority (GEPA) 2024 Non-Traditional Exports report/statistics
a4207.name: Ghana Export Promotion Authority (GEPA) 2024 Non-Traditional Exports report/statistics
a4207.speech: Revealed the country’s export earnings as $3,830,806,432 compared to $3,944,146,727 in 2023, a 2.87% dip, with the marginal dip primarily linked to reduced exports in iron and steel products to the ECOWAS region; indicated that between 2020 and 2024, NTEs achieved an average annual growth rate of 6.01%, accounting for 18.75% of total merchandise exports in 2024.

a4207.speaker: Francis Kojo Kwarteng Arthur, Chief Executive Officer of the Ghana Export Promotion Authority (GEPA)
a4207.name: Francis Kojo Kwarteng Arthur
a4207.title: Chief Executive Officer of the Ghana Export Promotion Authority (GEPA)
a4207.speech: Said despite a slight decline in NTEs in 2024, NTEs remained a crucial part of Ghana’s export portfolio, and that Ghana’s NTEs reached African markets with very strong performance ; “In fact, Africa accounted for 45% of all NTEs, with the ECOWAS region making up over 94% of Ghana’s exports to the AfCFTA market. This report is not just a record of export figures, it is a confirmation to the vision, innovation and perseverance of Ghanaian exporters. It tells a story of how Ghana continues to assert itself on the global stage, despite economic headwinds and shifting market dynamics” ; “The Manufactures and Semi-Processed sectors remain the backbone of our exports, contributing over 83% to total earnings. Of particular interest is the performance of cocoa paste, which grew by 35.54%, driven by robust demand from Europe and North America” ; noted that the NTEs performance highlighted Ghana’s competitive edge in value-added cocoa products ; “The Agricultural sector increased its contribution to 13.48% while the Industrial Arts and Crafts sector recorded significant growth of nearly 23%, a powerful reminder of the global appetite for Ghana’s creative and cultural exports” ; said the NTEs earnings affirmed GEPA’s strategy to deepen regional trade and leverage trade protocols and regimes like the ECOWAS Trade Liberalisation Scheme and AfCFTA ; “Looking ahead, GEPA is committed to aggressively implementing the Accelerated Export Development Programme. We will expand our market intelligence activities, forge new trade relationships, and work with stakeholders to boost medical tourism, structured labour export and export offering in the IT-enabled services space” ; indicated GEPA’s ambition to partner with Ghanaian tertiary institutions to recruit and position students strategically within the African market, and encouraged every Ghanaian to continue to work together to diversify the nation’s export base and add more value to the products.

a4242.speaker: Salva Kiir, President of South Sudan
a4242.name: Salva Kiir
a4242.title: President of South Sudan
a4242.speech: Has directed Trade Minister Atong Kuol Manyang to boost investment and address economic challenges, as he endorsed the resolutions of the recently concluded National Trade Forum 2025.

a4242.speaker: Atong Kuol Manyang, Minister of Trade and Industry of South Sudan
a4242.name: Atong Kuol Manyang
a4242.title: Minister of Trade and Industry of South Sudan
a4242.speech: Presenting a report which outlined the forum's resolutions, said illegal taxes and excessive roadblocks were key issues undermining economic stability; explained that these barriers force traders to raise commodity prices to offset their losses, further reducing the purchasing power of ordinary citizens.

a4242.speaker: Office of the President of South Sudan (statement)
a4242.name: Office of the President of South Sudan (statement)
a4242.speech: Said President Kiir acknowledged these concerns and assured the business community of the government's commitment to supporting reforms that reduce trade barriers, stabilize markets, and restore investor confidence: “He emphasized the importance of empowering local traders and called on the Ministry to prioritize policies that benefit the broader population and stimulate economic growth.”

a4299.speaker: Reserve Bank of Malawi (RBM) Financial and Economic Review for Second Quarter
a4299.name: Reserve Bank of Malawi (RBM) Financial and Economic Review for Second Quarter
a4299.speech: Data show that tea output declined between April and June to 13.4 million kg from 18.2 million kg in first quarter and 12.6 million kg in the corresponding quarter in 2024, while earnings climbed to $1.8 million from $1.6 million ; reads the report in part: “However, tea sales increased to 1.6 million kg in the quarter under review, from 1.4 million kg sold in the previous quarter. Meanwhile, tea prices dropped to $1.1 [about K1 926] per kg from $1.2 [about K2 101] per kg in the preceding quarter.”

a4299.speaker: Tonda Chinangwa, Chief Executive Officer, Tea Association of Malawi
a4299.name: Tonda Chinangwa
a4299.title: Chief Executive Officer, Tea Association of Malawi
a4299.speech: Described the drop as seasonal largely because second quarters are associated with dry weather, thereby reducing tea output. He said: “This is the normal annual tea production trend in Malawi. Production is typically higher in the first quarter then drops during the second and third quarters, before picking up again in the fourth quarter. This pattern is mainly driven by rainfall distribution.”

a4299.speaker: Beatrice Makwenda, programme officer, Trust Africa
a4299.name: Beatrice Makwenda
a4299.title: programme officer, Trust Africa
a4299.speech: Said they have engaged in a number of initiatives to boost tea output to strengthen smallholder institutions: “The tea sector is decisively working towards improving both production and productivity by strengthening smallholder institutions and creating a conducive environment for social dialogue” ; said the changes in industry practice coupled with research programmes targeting modern varieties and technologies will result in ethical tea production, which will sustain current markets and open new opportunities.

a4299.speaker: Sangwani Hara, Chairperson, Tea Association of Malawi
a4299.name: Sangwani Hara
a4299.title: Chairperson, Tea Association of Malawi
a4299.speech: Is quoted as having told a tea testing event in London, United Kingdom last year that enhanced trade can provide a good alternative to aid and development assistance through increased exports of products like tea.

a4680.speaker: Zambia Medicines and Medical Supplies Agency (ZAMMSA)
a4680.name: Zambia Medicines and Medical Supplies Agency (ZAMMSA)
a4680.speech: Has assured of an uninterrupted supply of medicines countrywide as Government has a well-defined plan of buying drugs.

a4680.speaker: Bradley Chingobe, ZAMMSA senior manager corporate communications
a4680.name: Bradley Chingobe
a4680.title: ZAMMSA senior manager corporate communications
a4680.speech: Says the Ministry of Health has an annual procurement plan that forecasts drug requirements of the country; has allayed fears of any shortages of antiretroviral (ARV) drugs or essential medicines in the country following a reported pause of medical supplies support from the United States Agency for International Development (USAID) ; “The Ministry of Health and other stakeholders are meeting to plan and forecast on how we can deal with this issue and, therefore, there should be no worries because we had similar incidents,” citing the outbreak of cholera and COVID-19 pandemics that were effectively dealt with.

a4697.speaker: Jeremiah Koung, Vice President of Liberia
a4697.name: Jeremiah Koung
a4697.title: Vice President of Liberia
a4697.speech: On Tuesday, 12 November, addressed world leaders at the COP29 climate summit emphasizing the importance of the Loss and Damages Fund ; informed the Summit that Liberia will further increase its climate ambition at the time of the country’s third generation NDC, considering biodiversity protection, conservation of mangroves, freshwater ecosystem services, child rights, and human mobility ; advocated for stronger cooperative actions and decisions on Articles 6.2, 6.4, and 6.8 at COP29 consistent with the Africa Group’s position in operationalizing carbon-market and non-carbon market mechanisms.

a4697.speaker: Dr. Emmanuel Urey Yarkpawolo, Executive Director of the Environment Protection Agency (EPA), leading the Liberian delegation
a4697.name: Dr. Emmanuel Urey Yarkpawolo
a4697.title: Executive Director of the Environment Protection Agency (EPA), leading the Liberian delegation
a4697.speech: At a side event on 16 November announced that Liberia intends to engage in the global carbon market, noting that harnessing carbon trading initiatives could benefit local communities and support essential national development goals, including the expansion of renewable energy and road infrastructure critical to the country’s Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).

a4697.speaker: Liberia’s 2021 NDC Financing Strategy (document)
a4697.name: Liberia’s 2021 NDC Financing Strategy (document)
a4697.speech: Estimated $490 million to achieve Liberia’s climate and green growth ambitions through 2025; however, Liberia faces a funding gap of $460 million, including zero from the private sector.

a4697.speaker: UNDP
a4697.name: UNDP
a4697.speech: Commits, for Liberia’s NDC 3.0 submission in early 2025, to providing technical and financial support through a combined UN Country Team effort under the UN Resident Coordinator, to be realized through UNDP Climate Promise 2025 “Below 1.5 By 2025” ; reiterates its commitment to supporting Liberia in building capacities and implementing programs to fully unlock the potential of a green economy for the country.

a4697.speaker: Anthony Ohemeng-Boamah, UNDP Liberia Resident Representative a.i. (author)
a4697.name: Anthony Ohemeng-Boamah
a4697.title: UNDP Liberia Resident Representative a.i. (author)
a4697.speech: A Call to Action: says the Liberian Government must take bold leadership and align national policies with climate priorities and create an enabling environment for climate finance; that development partners should provide financial resources, technical expertise and build local capacity, accelerating international climate finance delivery and prioritizing vulnerable populations; that the private sector must engage by unlocking green infrastructure investments; and that civil society should continue to increase advocacy for climate justice and guarantee locally owned climate action plans.

a4758.speaker: Kenneth Ekman, AFRICOM’s Deputy Director for Strategy, Engagement, and Programmes (major general)
a4758.name: Kenneth Ekman
a4758.title: AFRICOM’s Deputy Director for Strategy, Engagement, and Programmes (major general)
a4758.speech: Brought attention to resilience – a quality he highlighted in a recent podcast discussing his leadership style; referencing the Air Force’s Comprehensive Airman Fitness Model, he emphasised the importance of consistent habits in overcoming high-pressure situations, and his “disagree and commit” approach resonated with the collaborative spirit required in international security partnerships.

a4758.speaker: Joseph Biden, US President
a4758.name: Joseph Biden
a4758.title: US President
a4758.speech: Extended condolences for recent flooding in northeastern Nigeria and commended Mr Tinubu’s leadership in securing the release of an American citizen, in his 29 October phone call with President Tinubu; the discussion also highlighted the broader scope of collaboration, including the Bilateral Liaison Group on Illicit Finance and Cryptocurrencies and shared interests in reforming international organisations to amplify African voices.

a4758.speaker: The White House
a4758.name: The White House
a4758.speech: Confirms that this dialogue reinforced the importance of US support in addressing Nigeria’s security and economic priorities, paving the way for continued bilateral cooperation under the incoming Trump administration.

a4927.speaker: Israel Defense Forces (IDF)
a4927.name: Israel Defense Forces (IDF)
a4927.speech: Said seven Israeli soldiers were wounded in an explosion targeting an armoured vehicle in Gaza City on Friday night, while operating in the Zeitoun neighbourhood.

a4927.speaker: Abu Obeida, spokesperson for Hamas's military wing
a4927.name: Abu Obeida
a4927.title: spokesperson for Hamas's military wing
a4927.speech: Warned that Israel's plans to occupy Gaza City would increase the chances of the group capturing Israeli soldiers and that any Israeli military operation would put the lives of remaining hostages at risk.

a4927.speaker: Wafa, Palestinian news agency
a4927.name: Wafa
a4927.title: Palestinian news agency
a4927.speech: Reported that the Israeli air force carried out strikes on tent encampments in Zeitoun and the al-Nasr neighbourhood of Gaza City on Saturday morning.

a4927.speaker: Gaza's health authorities / health ministry
a4927.name: Gaza's health authorities / health ministry
a4927.speech: Said at least 62 Palestinians had been killed across Gaza in the previous 24 hours ; reported on Saturday that 10 people had died as a result of starvation or malnutrition in the past 24 hours, including three children.

a4927.speaker: United Nations
a4927.name: United Nations
a4927.speech: Said on Thursday that the renewed bombardment has already caused more than 23,000 residents of Gaza City to leave ; says the number of aid trucks entering Gaza is far below what is needed.

a4927.speaker: Mirjana Spoljaric, head of the International Committee of the Red Cross
a4927.name: Mirjana Spoljaric
a4927.title: head of the International Committee of the Red Cross
a4927.speech: Warned that it would be impossible to keep Gaza City residents safe during a mass-displacement scenario: “It is impossible that a mass evacuation of Gaza City could ever be done in a way that is safe and dignified under the current conditions,” said Spoljaric in a statement on Saturday; she added that no other area in the Gaza Strip had the capacity to accommodate such a massive displacement, given the already dire shortages of food and shelter.

a4927.speaker: Israeli official (anonymous)
a4927.name: Israeli official (anonymous)
a4927.speech: Told the Associated Press on Saturday that Israel will soon slow or halt aid into parts of northern Gaza as it begins its Gaza City offensive; the official said Israel would halt airdropped aid into Gaza City over the coming days and decrease the number of aid trucks that entered northern Gaza.

a4927.speaker: Six European foreign ministers
a4927.name: Six European foreign ministers
a4927.speech: Condemned the continued Israeli-aid blockade and planned Gaza City operation on Friday.

a4927.speaker: Kaja Kallas, EU foreign policy chief
a4927.name: Kaja Kallas
a4927.title: EU foreign policy chief
a4927.speech: Said she was “not optimistic” that the EU would take any measures against Israel because of internal EU divisions: “I'm not very optimistic, and today we are definitely not going to adopt decisions … We are divided about this issue,” Kallas told journalists at a meeting in Denmark ; said on Saturday that EU foreign ministers urged the US to reconsider its decision to bar Palestinian officials from attending the UN general assembly.

a4927.speaker: Simon Harris, Irish foreign minister
a4927.name: Simon Harris
a4927.title: Irish foreign minister
a4927.speech: “If the EU does not act as a collective now and take sanctions against Israel, whenever will it. What more could it possibly take? Children are starving.”

a4927.speaker: United States government
a4927.name: United States government
a4927.speech: Announced it would not allow the president of the Palestinian Authority, Mahmoud Abbas, to travel to New York next month for the UN general assembly; it also denied and revoked the visas of about 80 Palestinian officials.

a4927.speaker: Hussein al-Sheikh, vice-president of the Palestinian Authority
a4927.name: Hussein al-Sheikh
a4927.title: vice-president of the Palestinian Authority
a4927.speech: Called the US decision a clear violation of international law.

a4927.speaker: Pedro Sánchez, Spanish prime minister
a4927.name: Pedro Sánchez
a4927.title: Spanish prime minister
a4927.speech: Called the decision “unjust” and expressed support in a phone call to Abbas.

a4989.speaker: Mohamed Siad Doualeh, Ambassador of Djibouti to the United States and Permanent Representative to the United Nations
a4989.name: Mohamed Siad Doualeh
a4989.title: Ambassador of Djibouti to the United States and Permanent Representative to the United Nations
a4989.speech: Said that this General Assembly is different and will be more important because of the Summit of the Future, "a unique opportunity for us, as member states, to reflect and, hopefully, to resolve the doubts and divisions that have undermined international cooperation and that have contributed significantly to the erosion of multilateralism"; cited the paralysis of the Security Council as one example ; "As Africans, we represent 28% of the United Nations and we have doubts about the UN's capacity to respond to our priorities. We see the reform of global governance as needing to be bold and transformative" ; said members of the African Group in New York contributed to the discussions on the Pact for the Future, which they hope will be adopted at this session.

a4989.speaker: Mohamed Siad Doualeh, Ambassador of Djibouti to the United States and Permanent Representative to the United Nations
a4989.name: Mohamed Siad Doualeh
a4989.title: Ambassador of Djibouti to the United States and Permanent Representative to the United Nations
a4989.speech: Said of the Sudan conflict: "it looks like the chronicle of a tragedy foretold. It was a largely avoidable and preventable conflict, but it broke out on 15 April 2023, more than 500 days ago, and the consequences for civilians have been devastating" ; said some analysts estimate the conflict costs the African continent about $18 billion a year and that the consequences for Sudan's economy are far greater ; recounted that IGAD, currently chaired by President Guelleh, tried to intervene early and agreed to send a troika of regional presidents to Khartoum, but the mission could not go ahead after Khartoum airport was destroyed; that in mid-July, in support of the Jeddah Agreement, a mediators' seminar was organised in Djibouti, joined by the UN special envoy Mr Lamamra, to harmonise viewpoints and develop a common narrative on the causes of the conflict ; said that after the August Geneva proximity talks the parties appear unready to stop fighting, with a deep-seated conviction that a military solution is possible, and that "we will have to persevere, to keep talking to the Sudanese leaders and tell them that, in the interest of the Sudanese people, there must be a rapid conclusion of a ceasefire in order to allow political discussions and the delivery of humanitarian aid to those who need it."

a4989.speaker: Mohamed Siad Doualeh, Ambassador of Djibouti to the United States and Permanent Representative to the United Nations
a4989.name: Mohamed Siad Doualeh
a4989.title: Ambassador of Djibouti to the United States and Permanent Representative to the United Nations
a4989.speech: On a possible international peacekeeping deployment: "As is often said, for a peacekeeping force to be deployed there must first be a peace to keep, and in the current circumstances I do not think that is possible. I continue to believe that a political solution to the crisis exists, and Djibouti and President Guelleh are willing to continue talking to the parties" ; said he hopes all external actors concerned by the conflict will use their influence to send the message that the solution is political, "because that is what the Charter obliges us to do. We must always seek a peaceful path to resolve conflicts."

a4989.speaker: Mohamed Siad Doualeh, Ambassador of Djibouti to the United States and Permanent Representative to the United Nations
a4989.name: Mohamed Siad Doualeh
a4989.title: Ambassador of Djibouti to the United States and Permanent Representative to the United Nations
a4989.speech: On the Houthi attacks: said Djibouti "is very concerned by the continuing attacks on merchant and commercial vessels. Not only does this disrupt trade flows, but it perpetuates an unstable and volatile situation in the Red Sea and the surrounding waterways" ; "We must continue to persuade and to pressure the Houthis to cease all attacks on national and commercial vessels", and devote effort and pressure to avoiding further escalation, warning that if the situation drags on it will certainly have an economic impact on Djibouti ; said "we should all invest in the peace process in Yemen under the auspices of the United Nations", which would help reduce the threat posed by the attacks.

a4989.speaker: Mohamed Siad Doualeh, Ambassador of Djibouti to the United States and Permanent Representative to the United Nations
a4989.name: Mohamed Siad Doualeh
a4989.title: Ambassador of Djibouti to the United States and Permanent Representative to the United Nations
a4989.speech: On mpox: said the COVID-19 pandemic showed that "the threat of disease, wherever it is, is a threat to security, to the economy and to health everywhere in the world", which is why the international community agreed on measures to strengthen countries' preparedness globally ; highlighted "the excellent work of Africa CDC", which proved its worth during COVID and in the guidance it gave African governments ; said the goal for African countries is that "we do not want to keep asking our friends for resources, expertise, models and manufacturing capacity to improve public health and manage emergencies; we would like to do it ourselves", but that for now "what we are doing at the moment is putting out fires, and mpox must be brought under control before it is too late."

a4989.speaker: Mohamed Siad Doualeh, Ambassador of Djibouti to the United States and Permanent Representative to the United Nations
a4989.name: Mohamed Siad Doualeh
a4989.title: Ambassador of Djibouti to the United States and Permanent Representative to the United Nations
a4989.speech: On the US presidential election: "First of all, I want to say that we admire this country, the United States of America. It is a leading world power, and the elections that take place in the United States are followed all over the world, everyone is holding their breath" ; "What I would like to say as an African ambassador is that I would like to promote a narrative of the continent, a continent full of hope, a continent open for business, a continent ready and able to build strong partnerships on the political, economic and security fronts with the United States. We simply hope that the two leaders in the race will have Africa in their hearts and in their minds."

a5029.speaker: Malawi 2063 development blueprint (document)
a5029.name: Malawi 2063 development blueprint (document)
a5029.speech: Outlines a path toward a self-reliant, industrialized, and inclusively wealthy nation; it envisions transformation built on three pillars: increased agricultural productivity and commercialization, rapid industrialization and value addition, and sustainable urbanization through economic hubs.

a5031.speaker: Lin Jian, spokesman for China’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs
a5031.name: Lin Jian
a5031.title: spokesman for China’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs
a5031.speech: “China supports this draft resolution and congratulates Algeria and the other Arab countries for their hard work on this matter” ; “We hope that the Security Council will approve it as quickly as possible and send a strong signal for the cessation of hostilities” ; “This draft text adopts a clear position, demanding a ceasefire and the extension of humanitarian aid to the Gaza Strip, which corresponds to the correct orientation of the Security Council’s actions” ; “At present, the conflict in Gaza is dragging on and causing a humanitarian crisis, which is why the international community expects the Security Council to fulfil its duties in practice and in a comprehensive manner.”

a5031.speaker: Jun Zhang, Chinese ambassador to the UN
a5031.name: Jun Zhang
a5031.title: Chinese ambassador to the UN
a5031.speech: “If the United States is serious about a ceasefire, then vote in favour of the other draft.”

a5031.speaker: The Arab countries, China and Russia
a5031.name: The Arab countries
a5031.title: China and Russia
a5031.speech: Considered the wording of the American proposal ambiguous and denounced the “hypocritical spectacle” of the United States while Gaza is “virtually wiped off the map”.

a5031.speaker: New draft Security Council resolution (text)
a5031.name: New draft Security Council resolution (text)
a5031.speech: The latest version, supported by the Arab group, “demands an immediate humanitarian ceasefire during the month of Ramadan (...), leading to a lasting ceasefire”, and also calls for the unconditional release of the hostages and the removal of “all obstacles” to humanitarian aid.

a5031.speaker: Hamas Health Ministry
a5031.name: Hamas Health Ministry
a5031.speech: According to it, the Israeli offensive in Gaza has already caused more than 32,000 deaths.

a5145.speaker: European Union (EU)
a5145.name: European Union (EU)
a5145.speech: has pledged to strengthen its economic partnership with Nigeria, especially in key areas such as investment, trade, and job creation.

a5145.speaker: Gautier Mignot, EU Ambassador to Nigeria and ECOWAS
a5145.name: Gautier Mignot
a5145.title: EU Ambassador to Nigeria and ECOWAS
a5145.speech: said the EU plans to improve the structure of its economic relations with Nigeria and remove obstacles that hinder investment and trade. He said this is imperative as “no agreement or dialogue framework” exists between both entities.

a5145.speaker: Gautier Mignot, EU Ambassador to Nigeria and ECOWAS
a5145.name: Gautier Mignot
a5145.title: EU Ambassador to Nigeria and ECOWAS
a5145.speech: said another strategy is to implement the Global Gateway investment agenda, which prioritises job creation and opportunities for young Nigerians in sectors like green economy, digital, agri-food, and health; he noted that the agenda is the EU’s new investment strategy aimed at connecting people and accelerating green, digital and inclusive transition in partner countries like Nigeria. “The EU recognises the importance of accelerating Nigeria’s industrialisation and maximising the opportunities for local added-value and job creation. With the Global Gateway Investment Strategy, the EU works in sectors crucial for the transformation and diversification of the Nigerian economy such as energy, digital economy, agriculture and food security. The flagship projects under the Global Gateway include inter alia Omi Eko (Lagos waterway transport), development of the renewable energy sector (solar, small hydropower), production of vaccines (MAV+), Erasmus+ and Horizon programs,” he said.

a5145.speaker: Gautier Mignot, EU Ambassador to Nigeria and ECOWAS
a5145.name: Gautier Mignot
a5145.title: EU Ambassador to Nigeria and ECOWAS
a5145.speech: reaffirmed the EU’s commitment to addressing the unique development challenges in Northern Nigeria. He said with a cooperation budget of €731 million in grants for 2021-2027, the EU aims to support sustainable development, reduce poverty, and enhance access to basic services in the region, and that the grants will be used to support initiatives such as emergency food assistance, health, protection, and shelter for displaced people and victims of conflict. “The EU recognises the importance of solidarity and remains committed to partnering with the government of Nigeria in assisting the people affected by conflict and violence as well natural induced disaster. Together with its Member States, it is one of the main humanitarian donors in Nigeria. This assistance saves countless lives every day,” he said.

a5145.speaker: European Civil Protection and Humanitarian Aid Operations (ECHO), citing the latest Cadre Harmonise projections
a5145.name: European Civil Protection and Humanitarian Aid Operations (ECHO)
a5145.title: citing the latest Cadre Harmonise projections
a5145.speech: says over 7.9 million people require humanitarian assistance in North-East Nigeria, with 4.8 million struggling to find enough food during the lean season.

a5145.speaker: Gautier Mignot, EU Ambassador to Nigeria and ECOWAS
a5145.name: Gautier Mignot
a5145.title: EU Ambassador to Nigeria and ECOWAS
a5145.speech: said the EU is eager to partner with Nigeria to address the complex issues surrounding migration; he said this partnership aims to cover all aspects of migration, including smuggling and trafficking of human beings, working with diasporas, pathways, readmission and reintegration of migrants, and that the key aspect of this partnership is the readmission agreement, which will pave the way for a more global partnership.

a5171.speaker: Seedy Keita, The Gambia's Finance Minister
a5171.name: Seedy Keita
a5171.title: The Gambia's Finance Minister
a5171.speech: Has said that overall budget deficit is expected to slow down to D5.1 billion. He said the overall budget deficit including grants stood at D7.2 Billion for the first three quarter of 2024. However he anticipates that with the expected disbursement in budget support in the last quarter and expenditure restrain, the deficit is expected to slow down to D5.1 billion by the year's end against the Budget target of D4.5 billion.

a5171.speaker: Seedy Keita, The Gambia's Finance Minister
a5171.name: Seedy Keita
a5171.title: The Gambia's Finance Minister
a5171.speech: “The Gambian economy has shown remarkable resilience in the face of global uncertainties. As a result, it is estimated to grow by 5.8 percent in 2024 compared to 4.8 recorded in 2023.” ; He said the improvement is due to a stable macroeconomic environment, strategic investments in infrastructural projects, increased productivity in agriculture, recovery in tourism, and resilient remittance inflows.

a5171.speaker: Seedy Keita, The Gambia's Finance Minister
a5171.name: Seedy Keita
a5171.title: The Gambia's Finance Minister
a5171.speech: On sector-specific developments, he said that crop production continues to underpin the agriculture sector growth due to support from Government and development partners. He said, “The livestock sub-sector is estimated to maintain an upward trajectory while the fisheries and aquaculture sub-sectors are estimated to recover from contraction on account of renewed focus on aqua-cultural development”. Overall, he said the sector is expected to grow by 6.6 percent in 2024. The industrial sector which was driven mainly by construction over the past years is estimated to register a growth of 0.8 percent. The slowdown, he outlined is mainly due to the completion of many high-impact public projects. However, private-sector infrastructure projects remain robust. He also said that domestic electricity generation is recording a gradual increase on account of new projects although demand continues to outstrip supply. He reported: “The mining sector is estimated to stabilize, while manufacturing growth is estimated to register moderate growth due to competitiveness challenges. The services sector is expected to register a strong growth of 8.4 percent in 2024 driven by tourism and trade”. He said this is due to targeted interventions by the Gambia Tourism Board (GTB) and rising consumer spending following price stabilization.

a5171.speaker: Seedy Keita, The Gambia's Finance Minister
a5171.name: Seedy Keita
a5171.title: The Gambia's Finance Minister
a5171.speech: On the prices front, he said “the sustained tight monetary policy stance has triggered moderation in inflation from 16.7 percent in January to 10.0 percent by September 2024” ; stressed that the implementation of the foreign exchange policy by the Central Bank of the Gambia (CBG) coupled with increased foreign currency inflows, restored exchange rate stability.

a5171.speaker: Seedy Keita, The Gambia's Finance Minister
a5171.name: Seedy Keita
a5171.title: The Gambia's Finance Minister
a5171.speech: He said that Public finances reflect mixed performances in 2024. The revenue mobilization reforms adopted and implemented by the Government are yielding significant results. He reported: “As of End-September 2024, domestic revenue collection for the first nine months of the year, amounted to D24.2 billion against the target of D23.1 billion. Tax revenues amounted to D13.24 billion, a 3.36 percent increase above projections”. He added that non-tax revenue, particularly administrative fees, reached D4.40 billion, significantly surpassing the target of D3.53 billion. Grant disbursement remains resilient, noting that revenue and grants outturn for the year are expected to exceed the target.

a5171.speaker: Seedy Keita, The Gambia's Finance Minister
a5171.name: Seedy Keita
a5171.title: The Gambia's Finance Minister
a5171.speech: Concerning expenditure, budget execution has been particularly difficult this year due to unanticipated spending shocks. These, he said include the intervention of the Government to the tune of USD20 million to pay NAWEC arrears with the independent power suppliers. He said: “Other expenditure pressures came from the hosting of a very successful OIC Summit. The anticipated financial support for hosting of the summit was not realized and the Government was obliged to bankroll expenditures related to the Summit”.

a5195.speaker: Oil Marketing Companies Association of Zambia (OMCAZ)
a5195.name: Oil Marketing Companies Association of Zambia (OMCAZ)
a5195.speech: Is optimistic that the oil prices on the local market are expected to reduce following the significant drop on the international market.

a5195.speaker: Kafuala Mubanga, president of the Oil Marketing Companies Association of Zambia (OMCAZ)
a5195.name: Kafuala Mubanga
a5195.title: president of the Oil Marketing Companies Association of Zambia (OMCAZ)
a5195.speech: In an exclusive interview with Millennium TV, said this situation will boost the economy ; is thrilled that the tumbling oil prices internationally could significantly reduce Zambia's import bill, freeing up more money.

a5514.speaker: Somalia and Ethiopia (joint statement)
a5514.name: Somalia and Ethiopia (joint statement)
a5514.speech: Said they would work together to resolve a dispute over Addis Ababa's plan to build a port in the breakaway region of Somaliland; the two countries' leaders said they had agreed to find commercial arrangements to allow landlocked Ethiopia “reliable, secure and sustainable access to and from the sea” ; in a joint statement released late on Wednesday, said they had agreed to start technical negotiations by the end of February next year, and to conclude them within four months, without going into detail.

a5514.speaker: Tayyip Erdogan, Turkish President
a5514.name: Tayyip Erdogan
a5514.title: Turkish President
a5514.speech: “This joint declaration focuses on the future, not the past,” Erdogan said at a press conference in Ankara afterwards.

a5514.speaker: Hassan Sheikh Mohamud, President of Somalia
a5514.name: Hassan Sheikh Mohamud
a5514.title: President of Somalia
a5514.speech: Said he was ready to work with Ethiopia.

a5514.speaker: Abiy Ahmed, Ethiopian Prime Minister
a5514.name: Abiy Ahmed
a5514.title: Ethiopian Prime Minister
a5514.speech: Welcomed Turkish efforts to resolve the dispute.

a5514.speaker: Government of Ethiopia
a5514.name: Government of Ethiopia
a5514.speech: Said in January that it would lease a port in Somalia's breakaway northern region of Somaliland in exchange for recognising the area's independence.

a5514.speaker: Mogadishu (Somali government)
a5514.name: Mogadishu (Somali government)
a5514.speech: Rejected the deal and threatened to expel Ethiopian troops who were stationed in Somalia to fight Islamist insurgents.

a5698.speaker: MoveOn (progressive public-policy advocacy group, protest call)
a5698.name: MoveOn (progressive public-policy advocacy group
a5698.title: protest call)
a5698.speech: "Donald Trump and Elon Musk think this country belongs to them. On April 5 we say: Hands off! Trump, Musk and their billionaire cronies are orchestrating an all-out attack on our government, our economy and our basic rights" ; "We are taking to the streets across the country in a non-violent protest. (...) Join hundreds of thousands of people everywhere, backed by more than 100 organisations, as we work together to stop this brazen power grab" ; "This day of mass mobilisation is our message to the world that we do not consent to the destruction of our government and our economy for the benefit of Trump and his billionaire allies. Across the country we are marching, gathering and protesting to demand an end to the chaos and to build an opposition movement against the plundering of our country."

a5698.speaker: Local US press
a5698.name: Local US press
a5698.speech: reported that organisers in Washington expect around 12,500 demonstrators, specifying that the event will be attended by several Democratic members of Congress and will take place near the National Mall.

a5698.speaker: A member linked to the initiative (anonymous)
a5698.name: A member linked to the initiative (anonymous)
a5698.speech: confirmed to Lusa that American activists living in Portugal are also organising protest actions against the administration led by Republican Donald Trump.

a5698.speaker: Terri Blakley, American activist from California living in Ericeira, Portugal
a5698.name: Terri Blakley
a5698.title: American activist from California living in Ericeira, Portugal
a5698.speech: "I have been an activist for more than 50 years, but I have never felt so frightened. If I am going to oppose what is happening and do what I think is right, I have to be able to defend my causes publicly" ; "Personally I believe this miserable coup spectacle can affect the whole world. That is why we hope to involve non-Americans here in Portugal as well" ; "The Portuguese understand what a dictatorship is. (...) And fascism seems to have become a global epidemic lately. So I believe that what we are doing with these protests is just the tip of the iceberg. And I hope it saves us from Trump and pushes people to react to figures like [Russian President Vladimir] Putin."

a5902.speaker: Donald J. Trump, 47th President of the United States
a5902.name: Donald J. Trump
a5902.title: 47th President of the United States
a5902.speech: Dubbed April 2, the date the tariffs took effect, “Liberation Day”, drawing a parallel to July 4, 1776 ; has threatened to raise tariffs even further if Canada and European countries attempt to collude against the US.

a5902.speaker: Donald J. Trump, US President
a5902.name: Donald J. Trump
a5902.title: US President
a5902.speech: The rationale behind these tariffs, according to Trump, is to bring manufacturing back to the US from Mexico, Canada, China and Europe, where it had migrated due to what he deems unfair trade practices; his strategy is designed to reverse this trend. He also views tariffs as a tool to generate revenue to reduce the national budget deficit.

a5902.speaker: Joe Biden, former US President
a5902.name: Joe Biden
a5902.title: former US President
a5902.speech: Described Trump’s administration as an “oligarchic regime”, citing the number of billionaires in Trump’s cabinet.

a5902.speaker: Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala, Director-General of the World Trade Organization (WTO)
a5902.name: Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala
a5902.title: Director-General of the World Trade Organization (WTO)
a5902.speech: Europe appears to have adopted a measured response to the high tariffs, likely in line with her counsel.

a5968.speaker: Abdel Fattah Al-Sisi, President of Egypt
a5968.name: Abdel Fattah Al-Sisi
a5968.title: President of Egypt
a5968.speech: Announced at Sharm El-Sheikh the holding of an international Conference for the reconstruction of Gaza in November.

a5968.speaker: Badr Abdelatty, Egyptian Minister of Foreign Affairs
a5968.name: Badr Abdelatty
a5968.title: Egyptian Minister of Foreign Affairs
a5968.speech: Called for active participation by Ankara, insisting on the consolidation of the Sharm El-Sheikh ceasefire agreement ; expressed the hope of "seeing active participation by Turkey in this conference as well as its support for international efforts aimed at rebuilding the Gaza Strip and consolidating stability in the region" ; stressed the importance of "the full implementation of the provisions of the Sharm El-Sheikh peace agreement, guaranteeing a permanent ceasefire and facilitating the delivery of humanitarian, relief and medical aid to the Gaza Strip."

a5968.speaker: Egyptian Ministry of Foreign Affairs (statement)
a5968.name: Egyptian Ministry of Foreign Affairs (statement)
a5968.speech: Statement reporting that the Egyptian minister called for active Turkish participation and insisted on consolidating the Sharm El-Sheikh ceasefire agreement, and that he stressed full implementation of the peace agreement's provisions.

a5968.speaker: Foreign ministers of Egypt and Turkiye
a5968.name: Foreign ministers of Egypt and Turkiye
a5968.speech: Discussed the results of the Sharm El-Sheikh Peace Summit and the agreement reached to end the war in the Gaza Strip, in accordance with the plan of American President Donald Trump, insisting on the need to consolidate this agreement and the truce in order to contribute to regional security and stability ; also examined coordination on regional and international matters, aimed at serving their common interests and strengthening security and stability, underlining the importance of intensifying their political, economic and investment cooperation, as well as promoting bilateral dialogue.

a5968.speaker: Local media
a5968.name: Local media
a5968.speech: Reported that the two ministers discussed the results of the Sharm El-Sheikh Peace Summit and the agreement to end the war in Gaza, in accordance with President Donald Trump's plan.

a6240.speaker: Akinwumi Adesina, President of the African Development Bank Group
a6240.name: Akinwumi Adesina
a6240.title: President of the African Development Bank Group
a6240.speech: Implored African nations to prioritise strategic trade and investment partnerships as against engaging in a tariff war with the United States; warned, while delivering the 14th convocation lecture of the National Open University of Nigeria, that the new U.S. tariffs could send shockwaves through African economies, weakening local currencies, increasing inflation and raising debt servicing costs: “This will send other shockwaves right through African economies. Local currencies will weaken on the back of reduced foreign exchange earnings. Inflation will increase as the cost of imported goods rises and currencies devalue against the U.S. dollar. The cost of servicing debt as a share of global revenue will rise as expected revenues decline. These global tariffs will also have significant indirect effects on Africa, as its exports to developed countries such as China and others in Europe and Asia will buy goods from Africa. This will be expected to reduce the amount of official development assistance that will come to us from those economies. Of course, today we have the Africa Growth and Opportunity Act. It’s a duty-free access of Africa to the rest of the world.”

a6240.speaker: Akinwumi Adesina, President of the African Development Bank Group
a6240.name: Akinwumi Adesina
a6240.title: President of the African Development Bank Group
a6240.speech: Emphasised that Africa’s trade with the U.S. is minimal and engaging in a trade war is unwise, and called for a recalibrated trade and investment partnership with the U.S., citing Africa’s vast potential in infrastructure, agriculture and minerals: “What is needed is more trade with the U.S. The current dynamics call for a recalibration of trade and investment between the U.S. and Africa, which would expand trade opportunities, therefore, between the United States and Africa. The U.S. has huge opportunities in Africa to invest from rail to ports, to corridors to agriculture, to processing, to critical minerals. And I think I would like to encourage that there be openness in dialogue on this tariff. I asked the Minister of Finance about that this morning, and that we should prioritise negotiations to make sure that Africa is not underserved in this shifting geopolitically driven economic and investment landscape. Africa should also tariff-proof itself for future jobs.”

a6240.speaker: Akinwumi Adesina, President of the African Development Bank Group
a6240.name: Akinwumi Adesina
a6240.title: President of the African Development Bank Group
a6240.speech: Urged African nations to “tariff-proof” their economies by focusing on domestic consumption, value addition and the effective implementation of the African Continental Free Trade Area, arguing that the era of aid is over and growth must now come through disciplined investment, better resource management, and improved governance.

a6240.speaker: Akinwumi Adesina, President of the African Development Bank Group
a6240.name: Akinwumi Adesina
a6240.title: President of the African Development Bank Group
a6240.speech: Emphasised that enhancing education and technological sectors is key to addressing Africa’s challenges, driving economic development and fostering a more prosperous future; according to him, by investing in education and technology, Africa can cultivate a skilled workforce, empower entrepreneurs, and position itself as a global player in the digital economy.

a6240.speaker: Akinwumi Adesina, President of the African Development Bank Group
a6240.name: Akinwumi Adesina
a6240.title: President of the African Development Bank Group
a6240.speech: “There is no doubt that development aid plays a significant role for many economies in Africa, especially providing much-needed support for vulnerable populations that deal with shocks. However, despite its benefits, aid is not the way to develop. Indeed, no nation has ever developed based on aid. Let’s cast our minds back to the challenge of COVID-19. Africa must be 100% self-sufficient in the manufacturing of vaccines and medicines. In a world where it is becoming increasingly difficult to know allies or where long-time allies suddenly shift their priorities, there is no substitute for self-reliance. Africa must therefore treat health security just like we treat national defense. We must ramp up public and private sector financing for research and development. Our universities must be supported very strongly to have world-class medical sciences facilities that will allow our countries to drive cutting-edge innovations in medicine and pharmaceutical sciences. We must then connect them to fuel the growth of medical and pharmaceutical industries.”

a6416.speaker: International Energy Agency (IEA)
a6416.name: International Energy Agency (IEA)
a6416.speech: Championed the exaggeration that green energy is on the precipice of replacing fossil fuels, having "turned from an impartial arbiter of energy data to the proponent of the far-fetched prediction that fossil fuels will peak within just seven years."

a6416.speaker: William Nordhaus, Nobel Prize-winning climate change economist (research)
a6416.name: William Nordhaus
a6416.title: Nobel Prize-winning climate change economist (research)
a6416.speech: "His research shows that we should do something about climate change: early cuts in fossil fuel emissions are cheap and will reduce the most dangerous temperature rises. But his work also shows that highly ambitious carbon reductions will be a bad deal, with phenomenally high costs and low additional benefits."

a6416.speaker: Special "Climate Change Economics" issue (peer-reviewed cost analyses of net zero)
a6416.name: Special "Climate Change Economics" issue (peer-reviewed cost analyses of net zero)
a6416.speech: "It shows that even with remarkably generous assumptions, the benefits of pursuing net zero will slowly inch upward over the century. By mid-century, the benefits — the avoided costs from climate change — could reach about one trillion dollars each year. But the costs would be much, much higher." Three different modelled approaches show far higher costs than benefits for every year throughout the 21st Century and far into the next; by 2050 the annual costs of the policy range between 10 trillion and 43 trillion dollars, or four to 18pc of global GDP. Across the century, the benefit is 1.4pc of global GDP, while the cost averages at 8.6pc of global GDP.

a6497.speaker: Antonio Guterres, United Nations Secretary-General
a6497.name: Antonio Guterres
a6497.title: United Nations Secretary-General
a6497.speech: “Financing is the engine of development. And right now, this engine is sputtering,” he said in his opening comments at the four-day Financing for Development meeting in Seville.

a6497.speaker: United Nations and Spain (conference co-hosts)
a6497.name: United Nations and Spain (conference co-hosts)
a6497.speech: Believe the meeting is an opportunity to close the staggering $4 trillion annual financing gap to promote development, bring millions of people out of poverty and help achieve the U.N.’s badly lagging Sustainable Development Goals for 2030.

a6497.speaker: Pedro Sánchez, Spanish Prime Minister
a6497.name: Pedro Sánchez
a6497.title: Spanish Prime Minister
a6497.speech: Told the delegates that the summit is an opportunity “for us to raise our voice in the face of those who seek to convince us that rivalry and competition will set the tone for humanity and for its future.”

a6497.speaker: The Seville Commitment document (approved by consensus)
a6497.name: The Seville Commitment document (approved by consensus)
a6497.speech: Says delegates have agreed to launch “an ambitious package of reforms and actions to close the financing gap with urgency”; calls for a minimum tax revenue of 15% of a country’s gross domestic product, a tripling of lending by multilateral development banks and scaling up of private financing by providing incentives for investing in critical areas like infrastructure, as well as reforms to help countries deal with rising debt.

a6497.speaker: Rebeca Grynspan, U.N. trade chief
a6497.name: Rebeca Grynspan
a6497.title: U.N. trade chief
a6497.speech: Recently said “development is going backward” and the global debt crisis has worsened; according to her, last year 3.3 billion people were living in countries that pay more interest on their debts than they spend on health or education, a number that will increase to 3.4 billion this year, and developing countries will pay $947 billion to service debts this year, up from $847 billion last year.

a6497.speaker: Joao Lourenco, Angolan President, speaking for the African Group
a6497.name: Joao Lourenco
a6497.title: Angolan President, speaking for the African Group
a6497.speech: Said debt payment “consumes more resources than those allocated to health and education combined” for many countries.

a6497.speaker: Jonathan Shrier, U.S. diplomat
a6497.name: Jonathan Shrier
a6497.title: U.S. diplomat
a6497.speech: Told the June 17 meeting that “our commitment to international cooperation and long-term economic development remains steadfast”, but said the text “crosses many of our red lines”, including interfering with the governance of international financial institutions, tripling the annual lending capacity of multilateral development banks and proposals envisioning a role for the U.N. in the global debt architecture; also objected to proposals on trade, tax and innovation that are not in line with U.S. policy, as well as language on a U.N. framework convention on international tax cooperation.

a6497.speaker: Amina Mohammed, U.N. Deputy Secretary-General
a6497.name: Amina Mohammed
a6497.title: U.N. Deputy Secretary-General
a6497.speech: Last week called the U.S. withdrawal from the conference “unfortunate,” adding that after Seville, “we will engage again with the U.S. and hope that we can make the case that they be part of the success of pulling millions of people out of poverty.”

a6497.speaker: Ursula von der Leyen, European Commission President
a6497.name: Ursula von der Leyen
a6497.title: European Commission President
a6497.speech: Reaffirmed the bloc’s commitment to development financing, saying, “Our commitment is here to stay.”

a6520.speaker: Standard Bank Plc
a6520.name: Standard Bank Plc
a6520.speech: Welcomes the new administration's resolve for a return to economic stability, predictability and strong governance, and looks forward to partnering government and other key stakeholders to support the new President Arthur Peter Mutharika's plan to immediately tackle prevailing macro-economic challenges.

a6520.speaker: Phillip Madinga, Standard Bank Chief Executive
a6520.name: Phillip Madinga
a6520.title: Standard Bank Chief Executive
a6520.speech: “Attracting FDI from key economies such as the U.S and China, as outlined in his Excellency Professor President Arthur Mutharika's inauguration speech, is also critical in unlocking Malawi' growth potential and delivering meaningful economic recovery.” ; “We also note the President's determination to seek a renewal of relations with the U.S through his special friendship with the U.S President Donald Trump”.

a6520.speaker: Phillip Madinga, Standard Bank Chief Executive
a6520.name: Phillip Madinga
a6520.title: Standard Bank Chief Executive
a6520.speech: “Easing diplomatic hurdles with U.S should set the stage for dialogue aimed at finding solutions for Malawi's economy, trade and diplomatic relations.” ; “The loss of development and technical support following USAID's departure would require dialogue aimed at exploring solutions for the country”.

a6520.speaker: Phillip Madinga, Standard Bank Chief Executive
a6520.name: Phillip Madinga
a6520.title: Standard Bank Chief Executive
a6520.speech: “We look forward to a strong private and public partnership in the next critical three months of the government's transition process.” ; “The stage should be prepared for a re-set of a new economic trajectory where Malawi's resolve to return to stability through fiscal discipline and governance, dialogue with bilateral and multilateral donors and creditors and improved trade relations, is unambiguous”.
