a6581.speaker: Iveth Maibasse, Mozambique's Minister of Land and Environment
a6581.name: Iveth Maibasse
a6581.title: Mozambique's Minister of Land and Environment
a6581.speech: "With their identification, Mozambique becomes the first country in the world to apply the new global standard of the International Union of Nature Conservation to all its territory. That standard allows the identification of the main planet locations for species and their habitats."

a6581.speaker: Information revealed at the ceremony in Maputo
a6581.name: Information revealed at the ceremony in Maputo
a6581.speech: According to the information revealed at the ceremony, the mapped areas, 25 on land and 4 in the sea, occupy about 140,000 square kilometres in total and are pointed to as key for the improvement and health of populations who depend on biodiversity-related income generation.

a6581.speaker: Wildlife Conservation Society (WCS) (@TheWCS, Twitter post)
a6581.name: Wildlife Conservation Society (WCS) (@TheWCS
a6581.title: Twitter post)
a6581.speech: "Congratulations to Mozambique, which has completed the process of identifying and mapping 29 Key Biodiversity Areas. Watch today's ceremony via @WCSMozambique."

a6765.speaker: Akim Soul Guindo (Ibrahim Guindo), fashion designer and cultural operator
a6765.name: Akim Soul Guindo (Ibrahim Guindo)
a6765.title: fashion designer and cultural operator
a6765.speech: "As soon as people see an NGO in Mali, they say to themselves that there are millions involved and that they must go after their share..."

a6765.speaker: Akim Soul Guindo (Ibrahim Guindo), fashion designer and cultural operator
a6765.name: Akim Soul Guindo (Ibrahim Guindo)
a6765.title: fashion designer and cultural operator
a6765.speech: Stressed on social media: "I was very honoured to take part, and I recalled how much international cooperation, when it is well told, can help strengthen the image of a resilient Mali, in solidarity and in action."

a6765.speaker: El Hadj Djime Kante, president of the Global Health and Solidarity Association (AGSS/humanitarian)
a6765.name: El Hadj Djime Kante
a6765.title: president of the Global Health and Solidarity Association (AGSS/humanitarian)
a6765.speech: "This meeting allowed me to understand that international NGOs are useful, indeed indispensable, for the strengthening of peace in Mali, for the development of our country and above all for humanitarian work" ; "they are in Mali at our country's invitation, and therefore they have not been driven out of Mali... At the FONGIM cafe, we talked about the field, impact, commitment... but also received ideas. It was a rich, sincere morning, full of truths to be heard and shared."

a6765.speaker: El Hadj Djime Kante, president of the Global Health and Solidarity Association (AGSS/humanitarian)
a6765.name: El Hadj Djime Kante
a6765.title: president of the Global Health and Solidarity Association (AGSS/humanitarian)
a6765.speech: Confessed: "I spoke before a large crowd. I called the international NGOs every name under the sun. What is said behind their backs in our chats at the Grin, I said it in front of the representatives of the 110 international NGOs grouped within FONGIM. I felt a little ashamed afterwards because I was mistaken. The international NGOs work with our authorities in full legality and not against them" ; "at this cafe, I said out loud what many think quietly. A real mistrust fed by persistent perceptions and received ideas that are still deeply rooted. But that is exactly what this cafe was: telling each other things, confronting visions and opening a space of clarity."

a6765.speaker: Sidibe Kadiatou Cisse, country director of CARE International Mali
a6765.name: Sidibe Kadiatou Cisse
a6765.title: country director of CARE International Mali
a6765.speech: "NGOs are not meant to substitute for the State... They come to strengthen capacities and enable communities to assume their responsibility in managing what belongs to them" ; denounced that "the rumours come from those who stay in Bamako, far from the field and from the reality of the communities."

a6765.speaker: A participant (anonymous)
a6765.name: A participant (anonymous)
a6765.speech: "With everything that was said during this session, we understood that behind the smile of many children, women and vulnerable people there in fact lies an NGO that communicates very little about its achievements, believing that it was up to the beneficiaries to do so."

a6765.speaker: Mamadou Diop, president of FONGIM and country director of Action Against Hunger (ACF)
a6765.name: Mamadou Diop
a6765.title: president of FONGIM and country director of Action Against Hunger (ACF)
a6765.speech: Announced that these exchanges would be made permanent in order to bring NGOs and people closer together.

a6875.speaker: Arlindo Barreto, Rector of the University of Cabo Verde
a6875.name: Arlindo Barreto
a6875.title: Rector of the University of Cabo Verde
a6875.speech: argues, on the one hand, for the need to adapt teaching to the new times and “to the way the new generation perceives the world” and, on the other, for the importance of keeping what is “essential and perennial” for the development of critical thinking; also addresses the effects of the inappropriate use of screens, which shape brains and affect reading and concentration skills; and holds that the quality of education, preparation and the building of competences in students is a collective work, involving various actors and going far beyond the classroom.

a6875.speaker: Report prepared by a technical officer of the Oeiras Municipal Council (Portugal) at the request of the Brava Municipal Council
a6875.name: Report prepared by a technical officer of the Oeiras Municipal Council (Portugal) at the request of the Brava Municipal Council
a6875.speech: highlights problems such as school dropout and the reduction of the island's population.

a6875.speaker: Francisco Tavares, mayor of Brava
a6875.name: Francisco Tavares
a6875.title: mayor of Brava
a6875.speech: argues that rather than looking at the negative aspects it is necessary to see the positive aspects that the document highlights.

a6875.speaker: RCR Airways (statement)
a6875.name: RCR Airways (statement)
a6875.speech: issued a statement in which it clarifies that it wants to provide, among other things, air taxi and medical evacuation services in Cabo Verde.

a6875.speaker: Civil Aviation Agency of Cabo Verde
a6875.name: Civil Aviation Agency of Cabo Verde
a6875.speech: has not yet received an application for an Air Operator Certificate and the corresponding Licence to Operate Air Transport Activity for commercial purposes.

a6875.speaker: Olavo Correia, Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Finance of Cabo Verde
a6875.name: Olavo Correia
a6875.title: Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Finance of Cabo Verde
a6875.speech: announced that the third Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC) compact will prioritise connectivity and mobility in various dimensions — land, air, maritime, digital and human.

a6875.speaker: Adriano Moreno, national director of Education
a6875.name: Adriano Moreno
a6875.title: national director of Education
a6875.speech: explained to Expresso das Ilhas that voluntary contributions are not mandatory and must be agreed in formal meetings of the school council, where parents and teachers are represented.

a6875.speaker: Bank of Cabo Verde (Report on Economic and Financial Indicators; behavioural supervision report)
a6875.name: Bank of Cabo Verde (Report on Economic and Financial Indicators; behavioural supervision report)
a6875.speech: the economic and financial indicators published by the Central Bank state that the Cape Verdean economy grew between April and June this year, but less than in the first three months of 2024; according to the behavioural supervision report, in 2023 the BCV received 211 complaints from financial consumers – 197 related to the banking sector and 14 to the insurance sector.

a6956.speaker: Albert Ouedraogo, Prime Minister of Burkina Faso
a6956.name: Albert Ouedraogo
a6956.title: Prime Minister of Burkina Faso
a6956.speech: "Allow me, before answering, to greet Burkinabe at home and abroad. To greet, in the name of His Excellency the President of Faso, all our compatriots in the towns and the countryside who are living through this difficult situation... I would like a special thought for the internally displaced persons (IDPs), the Defence and Security Forces (FDS), the Volunteers for the Defence of the Homeland (VDP)... I would like to express all the compassion and solidarity of the government towards all the victims. I would also like to greet and thank the friends of Burkina who, despite this difficult situation, continue to accompany us... I am a Prime Minister so conscious of the stakes of his mission and I want to assure you that I am more than ever determined to wage this fight with the people until final victory."

a6956.speaker: Albert Ouedraogo, Prime Minister of Burkina Faso
a6956.name: Albert Ouedraogo
a6956.title: Prime Minister of Burkina Faso
a6956.speech: On the patriotic surge: "This patriotic surge is being put in place. At government level we have taken the full measure of the situation. At the level of the different layers of society too, we see an awareness of this situation, a need and above all, we have observed here and there calls for national unity, for a sacred union around the government in order to succeed in this fight."

a6956.speaker: Albert Ouedraogo, Prime Minister of Burkina Faso
a6956.name: Albert Ouedraogo
a6956.title: Prime Minister of Burkina Faso
a6956.speech: On coming from the private sector: "Coming from the private sector is a major asset. First, because I do not belong to a corps within the State, which gives me a certain room for manoeuvre in terms of neutrality... most of my clients when I was a consultant were public bodies. So I have a very good knowledge of these structures... which means that today I am comfortable with the various files submitted to the government."

a6956.speaker: Albert Ouedraogo, Prime Minister of Burkina Faso
a6956.name: Albert Ouedraogo
a6956.title: Prime Minister of Burkina Faso
a6956.speech: On administrative sluggishness: "We have an administration inherited from colonisation. So it is essentially an administration of command and I note with bitterness that it is not a service-delivery administration... today we must move towards an administration of services. One of the major flaws of the public administration is institutional instability... The question of administrative sluggishness is a reality. I note with much bitterness that within the public administration some agents have not yet taken the measure of the situation, of the urgency we are in today. Some parts of the administration continue to function as if we were in a normal situation. Absenteeism, people continue to arrive late for work, files continue to be handled as before - it is truly regrettable." ; Also paid tribute to devoted civil servants and to previous governments' modernisation efforts, saying the Burkinabe public administration is somewhat ahead of others in the West African sub-region and even beyond.

a6956.speaker: Albert Ouedraogo, Prime Minister of Burkina Faso
a6956.name: Albert Ouedraogo
a6956.title: Prime Minister of Burkina Faso
a6956.speech: On his student-union past: "No, not at all... I was an active militant and for that I was a victim of repression. Because you will recall that in 1990 there was a strike at the university and I, with other comrades, was expelled, hounded and even hunted down. Unfortunately we lost a comrade who was murdered on 19 May 1990 and for whom justice has still not been done... I am speaking of Dabo Boukary. We continue to demand justice and I am happy to see that the 'Dabo Boukary' case is scheduled to be tried in September 2022. As for my appointment as Prime Minister, it is not a renunciation of my trade-union convictions. On the contrary... I would like to tell my former comrades, those still in that organisation, that I have not changed."

a6956.speaker: Albert Ouedraogo, Prime Minister of Burkina Faso
a6956.name: Albert Ouedraogo
a6956.title: Prime Minister of Burkina Faso
a6956.speech: On his teaching career: "Indeed I began teaching at the university in 1996-1997 after the master's degree I obtained in business management... I taught at the university but also in private higher schools... I do indeed have many former students who are executives in the public administration, but also in private companies, banks and even in the previous government as in the current one. So I am proud today to see that I was able to contribute something... I also have former students who have become professors; so the next generation is assured."

a6956.speaker: Albert Ouedraogo, Prime Minister of Burkina Faso
a6956.name: Albert Ouedraogo
a6956.title: Prime Minister of Burkina Faso
a6956.speech: On measures against terrorism: "When we took office, just after the first Council of Ministers, we were given a briefing on the security situation, notably the nature of the threat. At that Council, we were asked to take non-military measures, notably regarding the drying up of the sources of financing of terrorism... Among the measures there is the suspension of the importation of Aloba-type motorcycles and others. There are also measures relating to the circulation of these types of motorcycles, to the suspension of the importation of explosives... More recently we have added other measures, notably the securing of strategic sites... There is also the question of the reform of the Volunteers for the Defence of the Homeland (VDP)... The reform will consist in setting up communal patriotic watch and defence groups at communal level. We are targeting 304 communes... the composition of these groups must reflect the communal community diversity, because we have observed a kind of communitarianism that developed within the VDP, and that also created the perverse effects we know... it is envisaged to grant a minimum flat-rate allowance. For now we have projections of 50,000 to 60,000 CFA francs per month... there is a whole series of measures, the military ones namely the territorial meshing of zones of military interest which also constitutes the beginning of the recovery of the territory... At the Council of Ministers two weeks ago, we adopted the updated counter-terrorism strategy... The particularity of our government is that we have adopted a holistic approach. Every member of the government is aware that the security question concerns him."

a6956.speaker: Albert Ouedraogo, Prime Minister of Burkina Faso
a6956.name: Albert Ouedraogo
a6956.title: Prime Minister of Burkina Faso
a6956.speech: On who is attacking Burkina Faso: "We have two large groups. One group that is very active in the Sahel and a second that is inside the country... At the beginning of the terrorist threat the armed terrorist groups were made up essentially of foreigners. But today we know that for the most part they are Burkinabe and foreigners intervene only for certain specific, complex actions. The intelligence services have now been able to profile the terrorists... First, the religious profile, who defends his religion and thinks he can impose the Caliphate by arms and blood. There is the profile of the defender, whose community has sometimes been the victim of abuses, who takes up arms to defend his community... There is also the profile of the follower, who enters this fight simply as a fashion; we also note the profile of the opportunist who profits from this situation - I am thinking of the big bandits who have turned into terrorists... We can also add the profile of the coerced victim, people who were forced to join the groups. It is important for us to know all this."

a6956.speaker: Albert Ouedraogo, Prime Minister of Burkina Faso
a6956.name: Albert Ouedraogo
a6956.title: Prime Minister of Burkina Faso
a6956.speech: On the attackers' demands: "The demands are not very clear. Very few attacks are claimed; so we do not really have a clear idea of their demands. But we have an idea of their motivation, and I have just spoken of the profiles. To know them is one thing; to be able to counter the threat effectively is another."

a6956.speaker: Albert Ouedraogo, Prime Minister of Burkina Faso
a6956.name: Albert Ouedraogo
a6956.title: Prime Minister of Burkina Faso
a6956.speech: On why he believes the war will be won: "We have decided, under the enlightened leadership of His Excellency the President of Faso, to rely on two essential pillars. The first is military action, but we know very well that it has its limits. And as they say, the soldier's bullet kills the terrorist but does not kill terrorism. On the military side many efforts are being made to strengthen the numbers and the equipment of the Defence and Security Forces... The other pillar is dialogue, in which we place much hope. Those who attack us are for the most part Burkinabe. This allows us to say that we can talk to our brothers and tell them to come back to reason."

a6956.speaker: Albert Ouedraogo, Prime Minister of Burkina Faso
a6956.name: Albert Ouedraogo
a6956.title: Prime Minister of Burkina Faso
a6956.speech: On the dialogue process: "Allow me to come back to our philosophy of dialogue... With the dialogue process we have begun, we have chosen to talk to our brothers. For that, we have chosen to set up local dialogue committees for the restoration of peace. They are made up of resource persons, community leaders whom even the terrorists respect and are ready to listen to. That is the philosophy of dialogue. There is no question of us bargaining anything whatsoever. All we can accept is to guarantee them security and their reintegration and not to carry out reprisals. To date we have set up nearly ten local dialogue committees for the restoration of peace and it is working very well." ; "There are concrete results and enthusiasm... We are in a dynamic of demobilisation first, then de-radicalisation, training and reintegration... We have already set up reception centres for the socio-professional reintegration of demobilised persons. We place much hope in dialogue simply because many are caught up in the machinery. They do not know how to get out of it."

a6956.speaker: Albert Ouedraogo, Prime Minister of Burkina Faso
a6956.name: Albert Ouedraogo
a6956.title: Prime Minister of Burkina Faso
a6956.speech: On hate messages on social networks: "Absolutely. I entirely agree with you that these are messages that can disturb the dynamic of dialogue. And we take advantage of this interview to condemn once again these hateful messages and to call on Burkinabe to calm, to social cohesion and to the sacred union."

a6956.speaker: Albert Ouedraogo, Prime Minister of Burkina Faso
a6956.name: Albert Ouedraogo
a6956.title: Prime Minister of Burkina Faso
a6956.speech: On partnership with Russia and the diversification of partners: "We have had partnership relations with Russia for a very long time. On the question of partnerships, we have always said that we are in a logic of diversification. The diversification of partnerships rests on several principles. First, the principle of freedom. For us, it is to go to the partner that suits us, even at the risk of ruffling historic partners... Then, diversification is founded on the principle of sincerity. They must be sincere partners who really want to help us and we must be in a logic of win-win partnership. On the military question, the partnership must be founded on the principle of territorial independence. That is to say that in this logic of partnership, there is no question for us of foreign troops coming to wage the fight we are currently waging in place of the Defence and Security Forces... what is extremely important is that we can count on our own Defence and Security Forces, on the capacity for an endogenous construction of resilience and resistance."

a6956.speaker: Albert Ouedraogo, Prime Minister of Burkina Faso
a6956.name: Albert Ouedraogo
a6956.title: Prime Minister of Burkina Faso
a6956.speech: On a possible break with France and on aid: "Indeed, there are questions to be asked. I understand their demand because France is the historic partner and the first partner in terms of figures. But it must also be said that, as a predecessor said, aid must help to kill off aid. If for years this cooperation has not made it possible to kill off aid, questions must be asked. I entirely agree that today it must indeed be reviewed. It must also be said that we, as leaders, cannot continue to remain deaf and insensitive to these demands. We have important components of our people demanding it... I wanted to end by saying that there is no problem between the Burkinabe people and the French people... So the problem does not arise in terms of peoples or populations, but perhaps in terms of policy between governments and of cooperation relations."

a6956.speaker: Albert Ouedraogo, Prime Minister of Burkina Faso
a6956.name: Albert Ouedraogo
a6956.title: Prime Minister of Burkina Faso
a6956.speech: On the French ambassador's "useful idiots" remarks: "Like all Burkinabe, I was indignant and outraged by the remarks made by an ambassador as respectable as Mr Hallade, who represents a country as respectable as France, which we affectionately call the homeland of human rights, the homeland of freedom of expression par excellence. We took these remarks badly, but it must be said that the government reacted and I would not want to return further to the question. The government issued a communique and the person concerned apologised. But allow me to say one thing. We have an African youth, particularly a Burkinabe youth, that has become more and more conscious, enlightened and free of complexes. And those who have not yet understood that, they are the real idiots."

a6979.speaker: Daniel Aristi Gaztelumendi, Ambassador of the European Union to Burkina Faso
a6979.name: Daniel Aristi Gaztelumendi
a6979.title: Ambassador of the European Union to Burkina Faso
a6979.speech: Recalled the historic importance of the EU's 75 years, founded on key values such as peace, democracy, freedom, human rights, solidarity, economic progress and social justice, in accordance with the principles of the United Nations ; highlighted the excellence of the more than 60-year partnership between the European Union and Burkina Faso, mentioning the ECHO office for humanitarian aid to internally displaced people, the PAIC GC which has generated 5,000 jobs in the creative industries and cultural governance, and the Erasmus and intra-African mobility programmes ; specified that for the period 2021-2024 the EU's investment in Burkina Faso amounts to 300 million euros, about 197 billion FCFA.

a6979.speaker: Daniel Aristi Gaztelumendi, Ambassador of the European Union to Burkina Faso
a6979.name: Daniel Aristi Gaztelumendi
a6979.title: Ambassador of the European Union to Burkina Faso
a6979.speech: Expressed his profound desire to see peace return to Burkina Faso, wishing that the country might overcome the terrorist threat so that displaced populations could return to their homes and children go back to school: "We wish with all our heart that Burkina Faso rids itself of the terrorist hydra, so that displaced populations can return to their localities and the thousands of children go back to school."

a6979.speaker: Dieudonne Sougouri, chief of staff of Burkina Faso's Ministry of Foreign Affairs
a6979.name: Dieudonne Sougouri
a6979.title: chief of staff of Burkina Faso's Ministry of Foreign Affairs
a6979.speech: Offered his congratulations to the EU delegation and its member states, hailing the quality of the bilateral partnership, and insisted on the common values underpinning this sixty-year relationship: "The partnership between the European Union and Burkina Faso is excellent and some sixty years old, founded on common values of solidarity, peace, unity, freedom, social justice, in respect for our identities and our cultural diversities."

a7068.speaker: Michael Raynor, US Ambassador to Ethiopia
a7068.name: Michael Raynor
a7068.title: US Ambassador to Ethiopia
a7068.speech: "The U.S. Embassy is deeply honored by the opportunity to facilitate such a partnership, through an extraordinary initiative led by some of the world's foremost economic experts based at one of the world's foremost higher education institutions, Harvard University."

a7068.speaker: Michael Raynor, US Ambassador to Ethiopia
a7068.name: Michael Raynor
a7068.title: US Ambassador to Ethiopia
a7068.speech: Said that the accomplished team and proven methodologies under Haussmann's leadership have an extraordinary record throughout the world of supporting countries' efforts to identify promising areas of economic growth, to highlight constraints to such growth, and to devise strategies to address both the opportunities and the challenges.

a7068.speaker: Michael Raynor, US Ambassador to Ethiopia
a7068.name: Michael Raynor
a7068.title: US Ambassador to Ethiopia
a7068.speech: "Re-setting an economy of Ethiopia's size and complexity is far from easy work," he says, "But Ethiopia has much strength to build upon." ; According to the Ambassador, first and foremost it includes an exceptionally accomplished team of economic leaders and experts to drive this transformation; he said that even though the country registered positive economic and social growth recently, these gains were made at the cost of incurring significant external debt, and without commensurate progress in job-creation or private sector investment.

a7068.speaker: Government of Ethiopia
a7068.name: Government of Ethiopia
a7068.speech: Has expressed it is working on homegrown policies to improve the economy, and is working to undertake structural changes in its macroeconomic arena.

a7068.speaker: Yinager Dessie, Governor of the National Bank of Ethiopia (NBE)
a7068.name: Yinager Dessie
a7068.title: Governor of the National Bank of Ethiopia (NBE)
a7068.speech: Said the initiative is expected to contribute to the policy dialogue and to craft plausible professional recommendations for the new economic reform program, which the country started to implement very recently ; "This economic reform focuses mainly on monetary and fiscal policy stability, structural and sectoral transformation, growth, job creation and poverty reduction." ; "We believe our economic reform agenda, which is a homegrown program, will contribute to macroeconomic stability and growth." He expressed his hope that the US government initiative will support the implementation of the Ethiopian economic reform initiative.

a7068.speaker: Yinager Dessie, Governor of the National Bank of Ethiopia (NBE)
a7068.name: Yinager Dessie
a7068.title: Governor of the National Bank of Ethiopia (NBE)
a7068.speech: Went on to say that even though the economy has grown for 16 years it has also seen some macroeconomic imbalance such as poor export performance and tax collection that needs to be rectified within the coming years.

a7068.speaker: Yinager Dessie, Governor of the National Bank of Ethiopia (NBE)
a7068.name: Yinager Dessie
a7068.title: Governor of the National Bank of Ethiopia (NBE)
a7068.speech: Told reporters that the initiative started when Ethiopia asked for more help to strengthen its economy.

a7395.speaker: Alessandra Saibene, coordinator of MSF's emergency response
a7395.name: Alessandra Saibene
a7395.title: coordinator of MSF's emergency response
a7395.speech: “Given the scale of the emergency, and with so many people displaced from their homes in such a short space of time, getting shelter, essential relief items, water, hygiene and health services in place is a priority” ; “Most people left their homes in a hurry and arrived with nothing. Families are sleeping on the floor in vacant buildings, like schools or churches, and sometimes even on the bare ground outside with only banana leaves or a plastic sheet for cover.” ; “When so many people live together in crowded and cramped conditions, with limited access to clean water and insufficient latrines, the risk of outbreaks of communicable diseases is very high. We need to act quickly to improve the conditions in the sites where displaced people are staying, otherwise the situation will only get worse.”

a7416.speaker: Herman Halushchenko, Ukrainian Minister of Energy (on Facebook)
a7416.name: Herman Halushchenko
a7416.title: Ukrainian Minister of Energy (on Facebook)
a7416.speech: Lamented on Facebook on Thursday morning that “once again, the energy sector is under a massive attack by the enemy.”

a7416.speaker: Serhiy Kovalenko, head of the electricity supply company Yasno (on Facebook)
a7416.name: Serhiy Kovalenko
a7416.title: head of the electricity supply company Yasno (on Facebook)
a7416.speech: Reported on Facebook that there are “emergency outages throughout the country”, specifying that these could last at least until the evening.

a7416.speaker: Maksym Kozytskyi, governor of Lviv region
a7416.name: Maksym Kozytskyi
a7416.title: governor of Lviv region
a7416.speech: According to the governor, more than 500,000 customers in the western region of Lviv were plunged into darkness, and 215,000 inhabitants in the neighbouring region of Volyn.

a7416.speaker: Regional authorities of Rivne region
a7416.name: Regional authorities of Rivne region
a7416.speech: According to the regional authorities, 280,000 people in the Rivne region are without running water.

a7416.speaker: Oleksandr Senkevych, mayor of Mykolaiv
a7416.name: Oleksandr Senkevych
a7416.title: mayor of Mykolaiv
a7416.speech: Announced that trams and trolleybuses were not running because of the power cuts, and that schools would remain closed all day.

a7416.speaker: Russia (government)
a7416.name: Russia (government)
a7416.speech: On Tuesday, Russia had promised a “response” – without specifying its contours – to two further Ukrainian strikes with American ATACMS missiles against its territory in the preceding days.

a7416.speaker: Vladimir Putin, Russian President
a7416.name: Vladimir Putin
a7416.title: Russian President
a7416.speech: Warned Western countries, following the very first Ukrainian attacks carried out with Western missiles against Russian soil, that Moscow reserved the right to attack directly the countries that support Kyiv, or to fire once again its intermediate-range hypersonic missile “Oreshnik” against Ukraine.

a7416.speaker: Andriy Yermak, chief of staff of President Volodymyr Zelensky
a7416.name: Andriy Yermak
a7416.title: chief of staff of President Volodymyr Zelensky
a7416.speech: Said Russia “is continuing its tactics of terror” and wants to “wage war on civilians during (...) the winter”.

a7416.speaker: Russian Defence Ministry
a7416.name: Russian Defence Ministry
a7416.speech: Claimed to have destroyed 25 Ukrainian drones overnight over the Bryansk region, near Belarus, over Crimea and over the Rostov region (south).

a7416.speaker: Administration of outgoing US President Joe Biden
a7416.name: Administration of outgoing US President Joe Biden
a7416.speech: On Wednesday called on Kyiv to lower the minimum age for military mobilisation to 18 instead of the current 25, to compensate for the shortage of soldiers in the face of the advance of Russian forces, notably around the towns of Pokrovsk, Kurakhove and Kupiansk.

a7416.speaker: Senior official of the current US administration (anonymous)
a7416.name: Senior official of the current US administration (anonymous)
a7416.speech: Said on Wednesday, on condition of anonymity, that Ukraine was facing an “existential” crisis in recruiting new volunteers: “The truth is that Ukraine is not currently mobilising and training enough soldiers.”

a7416.speaker: Donald Trump, US President-elect
a7416.name: Donald Trump
a7416.title: US President-elect
a7416.speech: Announced the appointment of former general Keith Kellogg, 80, who has called on Kyiv to make several concessions, as envoy to end the war between Ukraine and Russia ; highly critical of the billions of dollars released by Washington for Kyiv, promised to settle the war between Ukraine and Russia even before being sworn in on 20 January, without ever explaining how.

a7416.speaker: Keith Kellogg, former general and Trump's envoy
a7416.name: Keith Kellogg
a7416.title: former general and Trump's envoy
a7416.speech: Has called on Kyiv to make several concessions.

a7523.speaker: Somali Constitution
a7523.name: Somali Constitution
a7523.speech: Provides a legal framework for the development and promotion of all Somali spoken languages, acknowledging the importance of preserving these linguistic heritages.

a7523.speaker: Abdiaziz Hassan Laftagareen, President of the South West State of Somalia
a7523.name: Abdiaziz Hassan Laftagareen
a7523.title: President of the South West State of Somalia
a7523.speech: Publicly announced that the Peace Institute will fold the Peace Week programs annually.

a7523.speaker: Abdiaziz Hassan Laftagareen, President of the South West State of Somalia
a7523.name: Abdiaziz Hassan Laftagareen
a7523.title: President of the South West State of Somalia
a7523.speech: In his closing address at the Presidential Palace, thanked attendees for their active participation and emphasised the need for continued collaboration to build a more inclusive and united nation; highlighted key moments of the week, such as the opening of the Institute for the Development of the Maay Dialect and the graduation ceremonies, and urged everyone to build on the momentum of Peace Week.
